board_events.text: Hydrocarbons: carbon and hydrogen only
Three great branches: aliphatic, alicyclic, aromatic
Aliphatic = open chains, split by saturation
Unsaturated chains: alkenes $C_nH_{2n}$, alkynes $C_nH_{2n-2}$
Alicyclic = non-aromatic rings (cycloalkanes)
Aromatic = specially stable rings (benzene)
Theme: unsaturation invites addition; aromaticity resists it

segments.text: <curious>Every organic problem secretly asks one question first: what kind of hydrocarbon am I looking at? Hydrocarbons are compounds of only carbon and hydrogen, and this whole chapter hangs on a single family tree.
The family splits into three great branches. Knowing where a compound sits on this tree tells you how it will behave before you write even a single reaction.
Aliphatic hydrocarbons are open chains, straight or branched, and they split by saturation. The saturated ones, with only single bonds, are the alkanes.
Alkanes follow C n H two n plus two. Every carbon is saturated, with no bond to spare. These are Sub-topic one.
The unsaturated open chains carry multiple bonds: alkenes with one double bond, C n H two n, and alkynes with one triple bond, C n H two n minus two.
Alicyclic hydrocarbons are rings that are not aromatic, chiefly the cycloalkanes, and they are the bridge we cross next.
Aromatic hydrocarbons, the arenes, are specially stabilised rings built around benzene. That is Sub-topic four.
<whisper>Hold onto one theme for the entire chapter: unsaturation invites addition, while aromaticity resists it. Almost everything else is just detail hanging off that idea.
<curious>हर organic problem सबसे पहले चुपचाप यही पूछता है: मेरे सामने कौन सा hydrocarbon है? Hydrocarbons सिर्फ carbon और hydrogen के compounds हैं, और पूरा chapter एक ही family tree पर टिका है।
Family तीन बड़ी branches में बँटती है। Compound इस tree पर कहाँ बैठता है, ये आपको एक भी reaction लिखने से पहले बता देता है कि वो कैसे behave करेगा।
Aliphatic hydrocarbons open chains होते हैं — straight या branched — और ये saturation से बँटते हैं। जिनमें सिर्फ single bonds होते हैं, वो alkanes हैं।
Alkanes C n H two n plus two follow करते हैं। हर carbon saturated है, कोई extra bond नहीं। ये Sub-topic one हैं।
Unsaturated open chains multiple bonds carry करती हैं: alkenes में एक double bond, C n H two n, और alkynes में एक triple bond, C n H two n minus two।
Alicyclic hydrocarbons ऐसी rings हैं जो aromatic नहीं हैं, मुख्यतः cycloalkanes, और यही वो bridge है जो हम अगले पार करेंगे।
Aromatic hydrocarbons, यानी arenes, benzene के around बनी specially stabilised rings हैं। ये Sub-topic four है।
<whisper>पूरे chapter के लिए एक theme पकड़ लो: unsaturation addition को invite करती है, जबकि aromaticity उसे resist करती है। बाकी लगभग सब कुछ इसी idea से लटका हुआ detail है।

board_events.text: Cycloalkanes: an alkane chain closed into a ring
Two H's lost on closing $\Rightarrow C_nH_{2n}$
Same formula as alkenes, but NO double bond
Named cyclo- + alkane: cyclopropane, cyclobutane, cyclohexane
Carbon prefers the tetrahedral $109.5^\circ$
Deviation from ideal = angle strain (Baeyer's theory)
Cyclopropane $60^\circ$, cyclobutane $90^\circ$ = badly strained
Cyclopentane nearly strain-free; cyclohexane puckers to a chair
Larger rings are NOT planar; cyclohexane is three-dimensional

segments.text: When an alkane chain closes into a ring, two hydrogens are lost. What you get is a cycloalkane, the alicyclic bridge between open chains and aromatic rings.
Losing those two hydrogens drops the formula to C n H two n. So cycloalkanes carry the same general formula as alkenes.
That is a classic trap. The formula matches an alkene, but a cycloalkane has no double bond at all. Same formula does not mean same structure.
They are named simply by adding the prefix cyclo to the alkane name: cyclopropane C three H six, cyclobutane C four H eight, cyclopentane, cyclohexane, and so on.
Now the physics. Carbon prefers its tetrahedral angle of one hundred nine point five degrees. In small rings the geometry forces the C C C angles away from that ideal.
That forced deviation from the ideal angle creates angle strain, and that is the whole heart of Baeyer's strain theory.
Cyclopropane, with an internal angle of sixty degrees, and cyclobutane, at ninety degrees, are badly strained and therefore relatively reactive.
Cyclopentane is nearly strain-free, and cyclohexane is the most stable of all, escaping strain entirely by puckering into a non-planar chair shape where every angle returns to tetrahedral.
So do not assume planarity for the larger rings. Cyclohexane is decidedly three-dimensional, not a flat hexagon.
जब एक alkane chain बंद होकर ring बनाती है, तो दो hydrogens चले जाते हैं। जो बनता है वो cycloalkane है, open chains और aromatic rings के बीच का alicyclic bridge।
वो दो hydrogens खोने से formula C n H two n हो जाता है। तो cycloalkanes का general formula alkenes जैसा ही है।
ये एक classic trap है। Formula alkene से match करता है, लेकिन cycloalkane में double bond होता ही नहीं। Same formula का मतलब same structure नहीं होता।
इन्हें बस alkane के नाम में cyclo prefix जोड़कर name करते हैं: cyclopropane C three H six, cyclobutane C four H eight, cyclopentane, cyclohexane, वगैरह।
अब physics। Carbon अपना tetrahedral angle, एक सौ नौ point five degrees, prefer करता है। Small rings में geometry C C C angles को उस ideal से दूर खींच देती है।
Ideal angle से वो forced deviation angle strain पैदा करती है, और यही Baeyer की strain theory का पूरा दिल है।
Cyclopropane, जिसका internal angle साठ degrees है, और cyclobutane, नब्बे degrees पर, badly strained हैं और इसलिए relatively reactive।
Cyclopentane लगभग strain-free है, और cyclohexane सबसे ज़्यादा stable है, जो एक non-planar chair shape में pucker होकर strain पूरी तरह escape कर लेता है, जहाँ हर angle वापस tetrahedral हो जाता है।
तो larger rings के लिए planarity मत मान लेना। Cyclohexane पक्का three-dimensional है, कोई flat hexagon नहीं।

board_events.text: Reactivity tracks ring strain
Small strained rings relieve strain by ring-opening addition
So a strained ring mimics an unsaturated compound
Strain-free rings (cyclopentane up) behave like ordinary alkanes
They undergo free-radical substitution, not addition
Strained rings add and open; relaxed rings substitute
With this map, each of the four sub-topics details one branch

segments.text: Here is the beautiful payoff: a cycloalkane's chemical behaviour tracks its ring strain almost perfectly. Strain is not just a stability label, it dictates the reactions.
The small, strained rings, cyclopropane and cyclobutane, relieve their strain by ring-opening addition. They pop open to get rid of the strain.
For instance, cyclopropane adds hydrogen over a catalyst to give propane, behaving almost like an unsaturated compound even though it has no double bond.
That is the key insight: a badly strained ring mimics unsaturation, because opening the ring releases stored strain energy the same way opening a double bond does.
The larger, strain-free rings, cyclopentane and above, behave like ordinary alkanes. With no strain to relieve, they have no urge to open.
So they undergo free-radical substitution, like halogenation in sunlight, rather than addition, exactly like their open-chain cousins.
One line to remember it all: strained rings add and open, relaxed rings substitute. Ring size tells you the reaction.
With this map in hand, aliphatic versus alicyclic versus aromatic, the four sub-topics that follow each become a detailed study of one branch of the tree.
अब सुंदर payoff: एक cycloalkane का chemical behaviour उसके ring strain को लगभग perfectly track करता है। Strain सिर्फ एक stability label नहीं, ये reactions decide करता है।
Small, strained rings, cyclopropane और cyclobutane, ring-opening addition के ज़रिए अपनी strain relieve करती हैं। ये strain से छुटकारा पाने के लिए खुल जाती हैं।
मिसाल के तौर पर, cyclopropane एक catalyst पर hydrogen add करके propane देता है, लगभग किसी unsaturated compound की तरह behave करता है, जबकि उसमें double bond है ही नहीं।
यही key insight है: एक badly strained ring unsaturation की नक़ल करती है, क्योंकि ring खोलने से stored strain energy release होती है, ठीक वैसे जैसे double bond खोलने से होती है।
Larger, strain-free rings, cyclopentane और उससे ऊपर, ordinary alkanes की तरह behave करती हैं। कोई strain relieve करने को नहीं, इसलिए खुलने की कोई इच्छा नहीं।
तो ये free-radical substitution करती हैं, जैसे sunlight में halogenation, न कि addition, बिल्कुल अपने open-chain cousins की तरह।
सब कुछ याद रखने की एक line: strained rings add और open करती हैं, relaxed rings substitute करती हैं। Ring का size आपको reaction बता देता है।
इस map के साथ, aliphatic बनाम alicyclic बनाम aromatic, आगे आने वाले चार sub-topics में से हर एक tree की एक branch का detailed study बन जाता है।

board_events.text: Rank cyclopropane, cyclobutane, cyclopentane, cyclohexane
Rule: more deviation from $109.5^\circ$ = more strain = less stable
Cyclopropane: $60^\circ$, deviation about $49.5^\circ$, most strained
Cyclobutane: $90^\circ$, strained but less than cyclopropane
Cyclopentane: angles near ideal, almost strain-free
Cyclohexane: chair restores $109.5^\circ$, most stable
Stability: $\text{cyclohexane} \gt \text{cyclopentane} \gt \text{cyclobutane} \gt \text{cyclopropane}$
Reactivity is the exact reverse: cyclopropane opens most readily

segments.text: Let us apply the strain idea to a favourite N E E T stability-ordering question. Rank these four cycloalkanes from most to least stable, using only the angle facts we just met.
The single rule is this: the further a ring's internal angle is forced from one hundred nine point five degrees, the more angle strain it carries, and the less stable it is.
Cyclopropane's angle is forced all the way down to sixty degrees, a deviation of nearly fifty degrees. That is the largest strain, so it is the least stable.
Cyclobutane sits at ninety degrees, a deviation of about nineteen and a half degrees. Still strained and reactive, but noticeably less than cyclopropane.
Cyclopentane's angles sit very close to the ideal tetrahedral value, so it is almost strain-free and comfortably stable.
Cyclohexane wins outright: it puckers into the chair, every angle returns to one hundred nine point five degrees, and strain vanishes entirely. It is the most stable of the four.
So the stability order is cyclohexane, then cyclopentane, then cyclobutane, then cyclopropane, from most stable down to least.
And the reactivity order is simply the reverse. Cyclopropane, the least stable, opens most readily, while cyclohexane just sits there being an ordinary alkane.
चलो strain के idea को एक favourite N E E T stability-ordering question पर apply करें। इन चार cycloalkanes को most से least stable rank करें, सिर्फ अभी मिले angle facts इस्तेमाल करके।
एक ही rule है: किसी ring का internal angle एक सौ नौ point five degrees से जितना ज़्यादा force होकर दूर जाता है, उतनी ज़्यादा angle strain वो carry करती है, और उतनी कम stable होती है।
Cyclopropane का angle पूरे साठ degrees तक force हो जाता है, लगभग पचास degrees की deviation। वो सबसे बड़ी strain है, इसलिए ये least stable है।
Cyclobutane नब्बे degrees पर है, लगभग साढ़े उन्नीस degrees की deviation। अब भी strained और reactive, लेकिन cyclopropane से साफ़ तौर पर कम।
Cyclopentane के angles ideal tetrahedral value के बहुत पास बैठते हैं, इसलिए ये लगभग strain-free और आराम से stable है।
Cyclohexane साफ़ जीत जाता है: ये chair में pucker होता है, हर angle वापस एक सौ नौ point five degrees पर आता है, और strain पूरी तरह ग़ायब हो जाती है। ये चारों में सबसे stable है।
तो stability order है cyclohexane, फिर cyclopentane, फिर cyclobutane, फिर cyclopropane, most stable से least तक।
और reactivity order बस उल्टा है। Cyclopropane, सबसे कम stable, सबसे आसानी से open होता है, जबकि cyclohexane बस बैठा रहता है एक ordinary alkane की तरह।

board_events.text: Two traps that catch students on cycloalkanes
Trap 1: $C_nH_{2n}$ is shared by alkenes AND cycloalkanes
Same formula does not mean a double bond exists
Watch out: cyclopropane even ADDS like an alkene, but from strain, not a $\pi$ bond
Trap 2: assuming every ring is flat
Cyclohexane is puckered (chair), not planar
Pro-Tip: planarity is safe only for the smallest rings

segments.text: Before we leave the classification, lock in the two mistakes examiners exploit most on cycloalkanes.
Trap one is the shared formula. C n H two n belongs to both alkenes and cycloalkanes, so the formula alone cannot tell you which one you have.
Pro tip: never infer a double bond from C n H two n alone. A cycloalkane satisfies that formula with a ring and zero double bonds. Check the actual structure.

And do not be fooled by reactivity either. Cyclopropane actually adds hydrogen like an unsaturated compound, but that comes from relieving ring strain, not from any pi bond. The behaviour mimics an alkene; the structure does not.
Trap two is assuming every ring is a flat polygon. That works for the smallest rings, but it fails badly for the larger ones.
Cyclohexane is the counterexample to memorise: it is puckered into a chair, decidedly three-dimensional, precisely so it can kill its angle strain.
So treat planarity as a fair assumption only for the smallest rings. Larger rings pucker on purpose, trading a flat shape for freedom from strain.
Classification छोड़ने से पहले, वो दो mistakes पक्की कर लो जिन्हें examiners cycloalkanes पर सबसे ज़्यादा exploit करते हैं।
Trap one है shared formula। C n H two n alkenes और cycloalkanes दोनों का है, इसलिए अकेला formula आपको नहीं बता सकता कि आपके पास कौन सा है।
Pro tip: अकेले C n H two n से कभी double bond मत मान लेना। एक cycloalkane उस formula को ring और zero double bonds के साथ satisfy करता है। असली structure check करो।

और reactivity से भी धोखा मत खाना। Cyclopropane असल में unsaturated compound की तरह hydrogen add करता है, लेकिन वो ring strain relieve करने से आता है, किसी pi bond से नहीं। Behaviour alkene की नक़ल करता है; structure नहीं।
Trap two है ये मान लेना कि हर ring एक flat polygon है। ये smallest rings के लिए चलता है, लेकिन larger rings के लिए बुरी तरह fail होता है।
Cyclohexane वो counterexample है जो याद रखना है: ये chair में puckered है, पक्का three-dimensional, ठीक इसलिए ताकि वो अपनी angle strain ख़त्म कर सके।
तो planarity को सिर्फ smallest rings के लिए fair assumption मानो। Larger rings जानबूझकर pucker होती हैं, flat shape को strain से आज़ादी के बदले देकर।

board_events.text: Alkanes: every seat is taken
Every carbon uses all four valencies on single bonds
No double or triple bonds waiting to react
Old name 'paraffins': Latin parum affinis, 'little affinity'
$n=1$ methane $CH_4$; $n=2$ ethane $C_2H_6$
'Unreactive' means toward acids/bases/mild agents, NOT oxygen or radicals

segments.text: <curious>Picture the simplest local train line: a single track, every junction filled in, nothing left to attach. That fully-occupied, nothing-left-over picture is exactly an alkane.
Alkanes are the saturated hydrocarbons. Every carbon has used up all four of its hands, its valencies, holding either hydrogen or another carbon through plain single bonds.
There are no double or triple bonds waiting to react, no empty seats. This is exactly why they are so sluggish.
The old chemists called them paraffins, from the Latin parum affinis, meaning little affinity. They are the wallflowers of the organic world: stable and reluctant to react.
The whole family obeys one tidy rule, the general formula C n H two n plus two, where n is the number of carbon atoms.
Put n equal to one and you get methane, C H four, the gas from marshy fields. Put n equal to two and you get ethane, C two H six, methane with one hydrogen swapped for a methyl group.
<whisper>But be careful with the word unreactive. It means unreactive toward acids, bases, and mild agents. Strike a match, and the same methane combusts violently.
<curious>सबसे simple local train line सोचो: एक single track, हर junction भरा हुआ, जोड़ने को कुछ बचा नहीं। वो पूरी तरह भरी हुई, कुछ-न-बचने वाली तस्वीर ही alkane है।
Alkanes saturated hydrocarbons हैं। हर carbon ने अपने चारों हाथ, यानी valencies, इस्तेमाल कर लिए हैं, या तो hydrogen या दूसरे carbon को plain single bonds से पकड़कर।
कोई double या triple bond react करने के इंतज़ार में नहीं, कोई empty seat नहीं। यही वजह है कि ये इतने sluggish हैं।
पुराने chemists इन्हें paraffins कहते थे, Latin parum affinis से, यानी little affinity। ये organic दुनिया के wallflowers हैं: stable और react करने में हिचकिचाते हुए।
पूरी family एक साफ़-सुथरे rule को मानती है, general formula C n H two n plus two, जहाँ n carbon atoms की संख्या है।
n को एक रखो तो methane मिलता है, C H four, दलदली खेतों वाली gas। n को दो रखो तो ethane मिलता है, C two H six, methane जिसमें एक hydrogen की जगह methyl group आ गया।
<whisper>लेकिन unreactive शब्द से सावधान। इसका मतलब है acids, bases, और mild agents के प्रति unreactive। एक माचिस जलाओ, और वही methane हिंसक तरीके से combust हो जाता है।

board_events.text: Climbing the alkane staircase
A stepwise family = a homologous series; members = homologues
Members differ only in chain length
Understand one alkane deeply and you understand them all
Graded properties: e.g. boiling point rises smoothly
Payoff of a homologous series: shared chemistry, graded properties

segments.text: Start at methane and keep swapping one hydrogen for a methyl group, and you walk up a staircase: propane, butane, pentane, each step adding exactly one C H two unit.
Such a stepwise family has a name: it is a homologous series, and its members are called homologues. Each differs from the next by a single C H two unit.
Methane, ethane, propane, butane, pentane. Line them up and the pattern is unmistakable, one C H two added at every step.
The beauty is that the members differ only in chain length. Their skeleton is the same idea repeated, just longer.
So once you understand one alkane deeply, you understand them all, because the only thing that changes as you climb is how long the chain runs.
That shared skeleton is why properties change smoothly along the series. Boiling point, for example, rises steadily as the chain lengthens, with no sudden jumps.
That is the payoff of every homologous series: shared chemistry with gently graded physical properties. Learn the family once, apply it everywhere.
Methane से शुरू करो और एक hydrogen की जगह methyl group डालते रहो, तो एक staircase चढ़ते जाओगे: propane, butane, pentane, हर step बिल्कुल एक C H two unit जोड़ता है।
ऐसी stepwise family का एक नाम है: ये homologous series है, और इसके members को homologues कहते हैं। हर एक अगले से सिर्फ एक C H two unit से अलग है।
Methane, ethane, propane, butane, pentane। इन्हें line में लगाओ और pattern साफ़ दिखता है, हर step पर एक C H two जुड़ता है।
ख़ूबसूरती ये है कि members सिर्फ chain length में अलग हैं। उनका skeleton वही idea है दोहराया हुआ, बस लंबा।
तो एक बार जब आप एक alkane को गहराई से समझ लेते हो, तो आप सबको समझ जाते हो, क्योंकि चढ़ते वक़्त बस एक चीज़ बदलती है, chain कितनी लंबी चलती है।
वही shared skeleton वजह है कि series के साथ properties smoothly बदलती हैं। Boiling point, मिसाल के तौर पर, chain लंबी होते-होते steadily बढ़ता है, बिना किसी अचानक jump के।
यही हर homologous series का payoff है: shared chemistry के साथ धीरे-धीरे graded physical properties। Family को एक बार सीखो, हर जगह लगाओ।

board_events.text: 'Straight-chain' alkanes are actually crinkled
A C-C single bond is a cylindrically symmetric $\sigma$ bond
Like two halves of a steering wheel about its column
Rotation isn't perfectly free: a tiny energy speed-bump exists

segments.text: Think about it this way: every carbon in an alkane is like the central pole of a tent, with four guy-ropes pulled out to the four corners, a perfect tetrahedron.
This is s p three hybridised geometry, tetrahedral, with a bond angle of one hundred nine point five degrees at every carbon.
Because that angle is one hundred nine point five degrees and not one hundred eighty, an alkane chain is never a straight rod. It zig-zags, like a string of folded carrom coins.
That single fact quietly explains a lot: it is why so-called straight-chain alkanes are actually crinkled, and why the molecule can twist about its bonds.
And twist it does. Because a carbon carbon single bond is a cylindrically symmetric sigma bond, the two carbons can rotate relative to each other almost freely.
Picture it like the two halves of a steering wheel turning about the column. Each frozen snapshot of that rotation is called a conformation.
But here is the seed of the next idea: the rotation is not perfectly free. There is a tiny speed-bump of energy to climb, and that speed-bump is the whole seed of conformational analysis.
इसे ऐसे सोचो: alkane में हर carbon एक tent के बीच के pole जैसा है, चार guy-ropes चारों कोनों तक खिंची हुई, एक perfect tetrahedron।
ये s p three hybridised geometry है, tetrahedral, हर carbon पर एक सौ नौ point five degrees के bond angle के साथ।
क्योंकि वो angle एक सौ नौ point five degrees है, एक सौ अस्सी नहीं, इसलिए alkane chain कभी straight rod नहीं होती। ये zig-zag करती है, मुड़े हुए carrom coins की लड़ी की तरह।
वो एक fact चुपचाप बहुत कुछ समझा देता है: यही वजह है कि तथाकथित straight-chain alkanes असल में crinkled होते हैं, और यही कि molecule अपने bonds के around twist कर सकता है।
और twist करता ही है। क्योंकि carbon carbon single bond एक cylindrically symmetric sigma bond है, दोनों carbons एक-दूसरे के relative लगभग freely rotate कर सकते हैं।
इसे steering wheel के दो halves की तरह सोचो जो column के around घूम रहे हैं। उस rotation का हर frozen snapshot एक conformation कहलाता है।
लेकिन यहाँ अगले idea का बीज है: rotation perfectly free नहीं है। चढ़ने के लिए energy का एक tiny speed-bump है, और वो speed-bump ही conformational analysis का पूरा बीज है।

board_events.text: Your alkane fact-sheet
Alkyl group = alkane minus one H: $C_nH_{2n+1}$ (methane $\to$ methyl)
Carbon degrees: 1 to 4 other carbons = primary to quaternary
Halogen: $F_2 \gt Cl_2 \gt Br_2 \gt I_2$; hydrogen: $3^\circ \gt 2^\circ \gt 1^\circ$
Torsional strain; ethane staggered-eclipsed gap $\approx 12.5$ kJ/mol

segments.text: Let us pin down the alkane facts you must be able to reproduce on demand. Treat this as your fact-sheet for the whole sub-topic.
The general formula for an acyclic alkane is C n H two n plus two, where n counts the carbon atoms.
Combustion of one mole of alkane follows this: C n H two n plus two plus the quantity three n plus one over two moles of oxygen gives n carbon dioxide plus n plus one water.
Geometry: s p three hybridised, tetrahedral, H C H angle one hundred nine point five degrees; typical bond lengths are C C one hundred fifty four picometres and C H one hundred twelve picometres.
An alkyl group is an alkane minus one hydrogen, formula C n H two n plus one. The suffix a n e becomes y l, so methane gives methyl, minus C H three.
Degree of a carbon: bonded to one other carbon it is primary, to two secondary, to three tertiary, to four quaternary. Terminal carbons are always primary.

Two reactivity orders to keep separate. The halogen's reactivity runs fluorine greater than chlorine greater than bromine greater than iodine. The hydrogen being replaced runs tertiary greater than secondary greater than primary.

Finally, torsional strain is the repulsion between electron clouds on adjacent carbons brought close by rotation. For ethane, the staggered to eclipsed energy difference is about twelve point five kilojoules per mole.
चलो वो alkane facts pin कर लें जो आपको demand पर reproduce करने आने चाहिए। इसे पूरे sub-topic के लिए अपना fact-sheet समझो।
एक acyclic alkane का general formula C n H two n plus two है, जहाँ n carbon atoms गिनता है।
एक mole alkane का combustion ये follow करता है: C n H two n plus two plus तीन n plus one बटा two moles oxygen देता है n carbon dioxide plus n plus one water।
Geometry: s p three hybridised, tetrahedral, H C H angle एक सौ नौ point five degrees; typical bond lengths हैं C C एक सौ चौवन picometres और C H एक सौ बारह picometres।
एक alkyl group एक alkane minus एक hydrogen है, formula C n H two n plus one। Suffix a n e, y l बन जाता है, तो methane, methyl देता है, minus C H three।
किसी carbon की degree: एक दूसरे carbon से bonded है तो primary, दो से secondary, तीन से tertiary, चार से quaternary। Terminal carbons हमेशा primary होते हैं।

दो reactivity orders जिन्हें अलग रखना है। Halogen की reactivity चलती है fluorine, chlorine से बड़ा, chlorine, bromine से, bromine, iodine से। जो hydrogen replace हो रहा है वो चलता है tertiary, secondary से बड़ा, secondary, primary से।

आख़िर में, torsional strain adjacent carbons पर electron clouds के बीच का repulsion है जो rotation से पास आ जाते हैं। Ethane के लिए, staggered से eclipsed energy का फ़र्क़ लगभग साढ़े बारह kilojoules per mole है।

sections.title: Preparing alkanes I: hydrogenation and reduction

board_events.text: Four reliable routes: start with two
(a) Hydrogenation: alkene/alkyne + $H_2$ over Pt/Pd/Ni
The metal surface adsorbs $H_2$ and activates the H-H bond
Pt/Pd work at room temperature; Ni needs heat and pressure
(b) Reduction of alkyl halides: R-X + Zn + dilute HCl
Not the fluoride; nascent hydrogen replaces the halogen

segments.text: There are four reliable routes to an alkane. Let us take the first two, both of which build an alkane by adding or swapping in hydrogen.
Route a is hydrogenation. Pass an alkene or an alkyne over finely divided platinum, palladium, or nickel together with dihydrogen.
Ethene plus hydrogen over the metal gives ethane. The multiple bond simply soaks up the two hydrogens and saturates.
Why the metal? The surface adsorbs hydrogen and activates the H H bond so it can add across the multiple bond.
Without the metal surface, the H H bond is too strong to break at moderate temperature. Platinum and palladium work at room temperature; nickel needs more heat and pressure.
Route b is reduction of an alkyl halide. Treat the halide, but not the fluoride, with zinc and dilute hydrochloric acid.
The nascent hydrogen generated in situ simply replaces the halogen, turning R X into R H.
Remember the small print: this works for chloride, bromide, and iodide, not the fluoride, and it is the freshly born nascent hydrogen that does the replacing.
एक alkane तक पहुँचने के चार reliable routes हैं। चलो पहले दो लें, दोनों hydrogen add या swap करके alkane बनाते हैं।
Route a hydrogenation है। एक alkene या alkyne को finely divided platinum, palladium, या nickel पर dihydrogen के साथ pass करो।
Ethene plus hydrogen metal पर ethane देता है। Multiple bond बस दो hydrogens सोख लेता है और saturate हो जाता है।
Metal क्यों? Surface hydrogen को adsorb करता है और H H bond को activate करता है ताकि वो multiple bond के across add हो सके।
Metal surface के बिना, H H bond इतना strong है कि moderate temperature पर टूटता नहीं। Platinum और palladium room temperature पर काम करते हैं; nickel को ज़्यादा heat और pressure चाहिए।
Route b एक alkyl halide का reduction है। Halide को, लेकिन fluoride को नहीं, zinc और dilute hydrochloric acid के साथ treat करो।
जगह पर बनी nascent hydrogen बस halogen को replace कर देती है, R X को R H में बदल देती है।
छोटी शर्त याद रखो: ये chloride, bromide, और iodide के लिए चलता है, fluoride के लिए नहीं, और replace करने का काम ताज़ा जन्मी nascent hydrogen करती है।

sections.title: Preparing alkanes II: the Wurtz reaction

board_events.text: Wurtz: welding two alkyl groups
Two alkyl halide molecules coupled by sodium in dry ether
Joins two alkyl groups $\Rightarrow$ even-doubled carbon skeleton
Two DIFFERENT halides give a messy mixture of three products
So Wurtz is clean only for symmetrical alkanes
Mnemonic: 'Wurtz Welds' the fragment into double the carbons

segments.text: Route c is the Wurtz reaction, and its whole personality is that it welds two alkyl groups together into one longer chain.
Two alkyl halide molecules are coupled by sodium metal in dry ether. The sodium tears off the halogens and lets the two alkyl fragments join.
Two methyl bromide plus two sodium in dry ether gives ethane plus two sodium bromide. Two one-carbon fragments become one two-carbon chain.
Because it joins two equal alkyl groups, Wurtz always builds an alkane with a doubled, and therefore even-numbered, carbon skeleton.
Here is the catch. Use two different halides and you get a messy mixture of three products, because both self-couplings and the cross-coupling all happen.
That is why Wurtz is only clean for symmetrical alkanes. In an exam, propose it only when the target is symmetrical and even-carbon.
A quick mnemonic to keep: Wurtz welds. It welds the alkyl fragment to a copy of itself, so the carbon count doubles.
Route c Wurtz reaction है, और इसकी पूरी personality ये है कि ये दो alkyl groups को जोड़कर एक लंबी chain बना देता है।
दो alkyl halide molecules को dry ether में sodium metal couple करता है। Sodium halogens को नोच लेता है और दोनों alkyl fragments को जुड़ने देता है।
दो methyl bromide plus दो sodium dry ether में ethane plus दो sodium bromide देता है। दो एक-carbon fragments एक दो-carbon chain बन जाते हैं।
क्योंकि ये दो बराबर alkyl groups जोड़ता है, Wurtz हमेशा एक doubled, और इसलिए even-numbered, carbon skeleton वाला alkane बनाता है।
यहाँ पेच है। दो अलग halides इस्तेमाल करो और तीन products का messy mixture मिलता है, क्योंकि दोनों self-couplings और cross-coupling सब होते हैं।
इसीलिए Wurtz सिर्फ symmetrical alkanes के लिए clean है। Exam में इसे सिर्फ तब propose करो जब target symmetrical और even-carbon हो।
रखने के लिए एक quick mnemonic: Wurtz welds। ये alkyl fragment को उसकी ही copy से weld करता है, इसलिए carbon count double हो जाता है।

sections.title: Preparing alkanes III: from carboxylic acids

board_events.text: Two acid routes: drop a carbon or double it
Decarboxylation: heat the sodium salt with soda lime (NaOH + CaO)
Strips one carbon $\Rightarrow$ alkane with one fewer carbon
Kolbe's electrolytic method: electrolyse aqueous carboxylate
Couples two alkyl fragments at the anode $\Rightarrow$ even carbons
Mnemonic: Kolbe doubles, 'Decarboxylation Drops one'

segments.text: Route d starts from carboxylic acids and comes in two flavours, and beautifully, one shortens the chain while the other doubles it.
First, decarboxylation. Heat the sodium salt of the acid with soda lime, which is sodium hydroxide plus calcium oxide.
Sodium acetate with soda lime on heating gives methane plus sodium carbonate. One carbon leaves as carbonate.
So decarboxylation strips one carbon away, giving an alkane with one fewer carbon than the acid you started from.
Second, Kolbe's electrolytic method. Electrolyse an aqueous solution of the carboxylate salt.
At the anode, two alkyl fragments couple, so Kolbe gives an alkane with an even number of carbons, just like Wurtz.
Lock the pair with a mnemonic: Kolbe doubles, decarboxylation drops one. Same acid family, opposite effect on chain length.
Route d carboxylic acids से शुरू होता है और दो flavours में आता है, और ख़ूबसूरती से, एक chain छोटी करता है जबकि दूसरा उसे double कर देता है।
पहला, decarboxylation। Acid के sodium salt को soda lime के साथ गरम करो, जो sodium hydroxide plus calcium oxide है।
Sodium acetate soda lime के साथ गरम करने पर methane plus sodium carbonate देता है। एक carbon carbonate की तरह निकल जाता है।
तो decarboxylation एक carbon छीन लेता है, जिससे जिस acid से शुरू किया उससे एक कम carbon वाला alkane मिलता है।
दूसरा, Kolbe की electrolytic method। Carboxylate salt के aqueous solution का electrolysis करो।
Anode पर, दो alkyl fragments couple होते हैं, तो Kolbe even संख्या के carbons वाला alkane देता है, बिल्कुल Wurtz की तरह।
जोड़ी को mnemonic से lock करो: Kolbe doubles, decarboxylation drops one। वही acid family, chain length पर उल्टा असर।

board_events.text: Substitution by a radical chain in sunlight or UV
Step 1 Initiation: light splits $Cl_2$ homolytically
Step 2 Propagation: $Cl^{\bullet}$ abstracts H, then methyl hits $Cl_2$

board_events.latex: \begin{aligned} Cl^{\bullet} + CH_4 &\rightarrow {}^{\bullet}CH_3 + HCl \\ {}^{\bullet}CH_3 + Cl_2 &\rightarrow CH_3Cl + Cl^{\bullet} \end{aligned}

board_events.text: The regenerated $Cl^{\bullet}$ repeats the cycle: that is the chain
Step 3 Termination: two radicals combine, e.g. $2\,{}^{\bullet}CH_3 \to C_2H_6$
Selectivity: $3^\circ \gt 2^\circ \gt 1^\circ$ (3 radical most stabilised)

segments.text: <excited>Now the signature reaction of alkanes: halogenation. A hydrogen is swapped for a halogen, and it happens by a free-radical chain in sunlight or ultraviolet light, in three steps you must reproduce.
Step one, initiation. Light or heat splits the chlorine molecule homolytically, each atom keeping one electron.
The chlorine chlorine bond breaks into two chlorine radicals. It breaks first because it is weaker than a C C or a C H bond.
Step two, propagation, is the heart of the chain. A chlorine radical abstracts a hydrogen from methane, and the new methyl radical then attacks another chlorine molecule.
Chlorine radical plus methane gives a methyl radical plus H C l; then methyl radical plus chlorine gives chloromethane and regenerates a chlorine radical.
Because the second step regenerates a chlorine radical, the cycle repeats over and over. That self-sustaining loop is exactly what we mean by a chain.
Step three, termination. Two radicals combine and the chain dies. When two methyl radicals meet, they give ethane, which is where the trace ethane by-product comes from.

The physical reason behind selectivity: a tertiary C H breaks most easily because the tertiary radical formed is the most stabilised, by hyperconjugation. That is why the order is tertiary, secondary, primary.

<excited>अब alkanes की signature reaction: halogenation। एक hydrogen की जगह halogen आता है, और ये sunlight या ultraviolet light में एक free-radical chain से होता है, तीन steps में जो आपको reproduce करने आने चाहिए।
Step one, initiation। Light या heat chlorine molecule को homolytically तोड़ता है, हर atom एक electron रखते हुए।
Chlorine chlorine bond दो chlorine radicals में टूटता है। ये पहले टूटता है क्योंकि ये C C या C H bond से कमज़ोर है।
Step two, propagation, chain का दिल है। एक chlorine radical methane से एक hydrogen खींचता है, और नया methyl radical फिर दूसरे chlorine molecule पर हमला करता है।
Chlorine radical plus methane एक methyl radical plus H C l देता है; फिर methyl radical plus chlorine, chloromethane देता है और एक chlorine radical फिर से बना देता है।
क्योंकि दूसरा step एक chlorine radical फिर से बना देता है, cycle बार-बार दोहराता है। वो self-sustaining loop ही है जिसे हम chain कहते हैं।
Step three, termination। दो radicals मिलते हैं और chain मर जाती है। जब दो methyl radicals मिलते हैं, तो वो ethane देते हैं, यहीं से trace ethane by-product आता है।

Selectivity के पीछे physical वजह: एक tertiary C H सबसे आसानी से टूटता है क्योंकि बनने वाला tertiary radical सबसे ज़्यादा stabilised होता है, hyperconjugation से। इसीलिए order है tertiary, secondary, primary।

board_events.text: Gap is tiny, so conformers cannot be isolated

segments.text: <curious>Hold one carbon of ethane still and rotate the other about the C C axis. The hydrogens sweep through an infinite set of arrangements, and two extremes matter.
In the eclipsed conformation, the front and back C H bonds line up exactly, at a dihedral angle of zero degrees.
There the electron clouds are closest, so repulsion and torsional strain are at a maximum, and the energy is highest.
In the staggered conformation, the back hydrogens bisect the gaps between the front hydrogens, at a dihedral angle of sixty degrees.
There the electron clouds are farthest apart, so torsional strain is at a minimum, the energy is lowest, and stability is greatest.
Plot energy against dihedral angle and you get this smooth wave: minima at the staggered angles, maxima at the eclipsed. Below the curve are the Newman projections that go with each.
The energy gap between them is only about twelve point five kilojoules per mole, a very small barrier.

That barrier is small enough that ordinary thermal collisions push the molecule over it continuously. So rotation is almost free and the individual conformers cannot be isolated; the molecule simply spends most of its time near the staggered shape.
<curious>Ethane के एक carbon को स्थिर पकड़ो और दूसरे को C C axis के around घुमाओ। Hydrogens arrangements के एक अनंत set से गुज़रते हैं, और दो extremes मायने रखते हैं।
Eclipsed conformation में, front और back C H bonds बिल्कुल line up हो जाते हैं, zero degrees के dihedral angle पर।
वहाँ electron clouds सबसे पास होते हैं, इसलिए repulsion और torsional strain maximum पर होती है, और energy सबसे ज़्यादा होती है।
Staggered conformation में, back hydrogens front hydrogens के बीच के gaps को bisect करते हैं, साठ degrees के dihedral angle पर।
वहाँ electron clouds सबसे दूर होते हैं, इसलिए torsional strain minimum पर होती है, energy सबसे कम होती है, और stability सबसे ज़्यादा।
Energy को dihedral angle के against plot करो और ये smooth wave मिलती है: staggered angles पर minima, eclipsed पर maxima। Curve के नीचे हर एक के साथ जाने वाली Newman projections हैं।
उनके बीच energy gap सिर्फ लगभग साढ़े बारह kilojoules per mole है, एक बहुत छोटा barrier।

वो barrier इतना छोटा है कि ordinary thermal collisions molecule को उसके पार लगातार धकेलते रहते हैं। तो rotation लगभग free है और अलग-अलग conformers isolate नहीं किए जा सकते; molecule बस अपना ज़्यादातर वक़्त staggered shape के पास बिताता है।

board_events.text: Non-polar molecules, weak forces
C and H differ little in electronegativity $\Rightarrow$ almost no charge separation
Held only by weak van der Waals (dispersion) forces
$C_1$-$C_4$ gases, $C_5$-$C_{17}$ liquids, $C_{18}$+ solids
Boiling point rises with chain length...
...but falls with branching (more spherical, less contact area)
Insoluble in water, soluble in non-polar solvents ('like dissolves like')

segments.text: The physical properties of alkanes all flow from one fact: these are essentially non-polar molecules.
Carbon and hydrogen differ very little in electronegativity, so the C C and C H bonds carry almost no charge separation.
With no real dipoles, the molecules are held together only by weak van der Waals dispersion forces, and every consequence follows from that.
The first four members are gases, the fifth to the seventeenth are liquids, and those with eighteen or more carbons are solids, because dispersion forces grow with molecular surface area.
So boiling point rises steadily with chain length: a longer chain has more surface, more contact, and stronger total dispersion attraction.
But boiling point falls with branching. A branched isomer is more spherical, has a smaller contact surface, and so its molecules separate at a lower temperature.
And being non-polar, alkanes are practically insoluble in water but dissolve readily in non-polar solvents. That is exactly why petrol, a mixture of higher alkanes, lifts greasy stains.
Alkanes की सारी physical properties एक fact से बहती हैं: ये असल में non-polar molecules हैं।
Carbon और hydrogen की electronegativity में बहुत कम फ़र्क़ है, इसलिए C C और C H bonds में लगभग कोई charge separation नहीं होता।
कोई असली dipoles न होने से, molecules सिर्फ weak van der Waals dispersion forces से जुड़े रहते हैं, और हर नतीजा उसी से निकलता है।
पहले चार members gases हैं, पाँचवें से सत्रहवें तक liquids हैं, और अठारह या ज़्यादा carbons वाले solids हैं, क्योंकि dispersion forces molecular surface area के साथ बढ़ती हैं।
तो boiling point chain length के साथ steadily बढ़ता है: लंबी chain की ज़्यादा surface, ज़्यादा contact, और ज़्यादा कुल dispersion attraction होती है।
लेकिन boiling point branching के साथ गिरता है। एक branched isomer ज़्यादा spherical होता है, उसकी contact surface छोटी होती है, इसलिए उसके molecules कम temperature पर अलग हो जाते हैं।
और non-polar होने से, alkanes पानी में लगभग insoluble हैं लेकिन non-polar solvents में आसानी से घुल जाते हैं। यही वजह है कि petrol, higher alkanes का mixture, greasy दाग़ उठा लेता है।

sections.title: The rest of the reaction map

board_events.text: Beyond substitution: five more reactions
Incomplete combustion $\to$ carbon black or carbon monoxide
Controlled oxidation: $CH_4$/Cu, 523 K $\to$ methanol; /Mo oxide $\to$ methanal
Alkanes with a $3^\circ$ H + $KMnO_4$ $\to$ tertiary alcohol
Isomerisation: straight chain + anhydrous $AlCl_3$/HCl $\to$ branched
Aromatization: $C_6$+ alkane, 773 K, oxides $\to$ benzene (n-hexane $\to$ benzene)
Steam: $CH_4 + H_2O$/Ni, 1273 K $\to CO + H_2$; pyrolysis cracks higher alkanes

segments.text: Beyond free-radical substitution, five more reaction types complete the alkane picture. Let us map them quickly.
First, combustion. Methane burns in excess air to carbon dioxide and water, releasing about eight hundred ninety kilojoules per mole. This is why alkanes are our dominant fuels.
With insufficient oxygen, incomplete combustion gives carbon black, used in ink and printer toner, or carbon monoxide.
Controlled oxidation stops the burn partway. Methane over copper at five hundred twenty three kelvin gives methanol, while over molybdenum oxide it gives methanal.
An alkane that carries a tertiary hydrogen is oxidised by potassium permanganate to the corresponding tertiary alcohol.
Isomerisation: heat a straight-chain alkane with anhydrous aluminium chloride and hydrogen chloride, and it converts to its branched isomers, the industrial trick for raising octane rating.

Aromatization, or reforming: an alkane of six or more carbons, heated near seven hundred seventy three kelvin over vanadium, molybdenum, or chromium oxides, cyclises to benzene. n-hexane goes to benzene.

Finally, methane with steam over nickel at one thousand two hundred seventy three kelvin gives carbon monoxide and hydrogen. And strong heating with no air causes pyrolysis, cracking higher alkanes into smaller pieces.
Free-radical substitution के परे, पाँच और reaction types alkane की तस्वीर पूरी करते हैं। चलो इन्हें जल्दी से map करें।
पहला, combustion। Methane excess air में carbon dioxide और water में जलता है, लगभग आठ सौ नब्बे kilojoules per mole release करते हुए। इसीलिए alkanes हमारे प्रमुख fuels हैं।
कम oxygen के साथ, incomplete combustion carbon black देता है, जो ink और printer toner में इस्तेमाल होता है, या carbon monoxide।
Controlled oxidation जलने को बीच में रोक देता है। Methane copper पर पाँच सौ तेईस kelvin पर methanol देता है, जबकि molybdenum oxide पर methanal।
जो alkane एक tertiary hydrogen carry करता है, उसे potassium permanganate corresponding tertiary alcohol में oxidise कर देता है।
Isomerisation: एक straight-chain alkane को anhydrous aluminium chloride और hydrogen chloride के साथ गरम करो, और वो अपने branched isomers में बदल जाता है, octane rating बढ़ाने का industrial trick।

Aromatization, या reforming: छह या ज़्यादा carbons का alkane, vanadium, molybdenum, या chromium oxides पर सात सौ तिहत्तर kelvin के पास गरम किया जाए, तो benzene में cyclise हो जाता है। n-hexane, benzene में जाता है।

आख़िर में, methane steam के साथ nickel पर एक हज़ार दो सौ तिहत्तर kelvin पर carbon monoxide और hydrogen देता है। और बिना हवा के तेज़ गरम करने से pyrolysis होता है, higher alkanes को छोटे टुकड़ों में crack करते हुए।

sections.title: CO2 volume from combustion of propane

board_events.text: [C B S E] Volume of $CO_2$ from 2.2 g propane at S T P
Given: 2.2 g propane; molar mass 44; molar volume 22.4 L/mol at S T P
Step 1: moles of propane $= 2.2 / 44 = 0.05$ mol
Step 3: 1 mol propane $\to$ 3 mol $CO_2$, so $0.05 \to 0.15$ mol
Step 4: volume $= 0.15 \times 22.4 = 3.36$ L
Answer: 3.36 L of $CO_2$ at S T P

segments.text: A clean C B S E numerical. Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide, measured at S T P, from the complete combustion of two point two grams of propane.
We are given: mass of propane two point two grams, molar mass forty four grams per mole, and molar volume twenty two point four litres per mole at S T P.
Step one, moles of propane. Two point two divided by forty four gives zero point zero five moles.
Step two, the balanced equation: propane plus five oxygen gives three carbon dioxide plus four water.
Step three, the mole ratio. One mole of propane gives three moles of carbon dioxide, so zero point zero five moles gives zero point one five moles of carbon dioxide.
Step four, the volume at S T P. Zero point one five times twenty two point four gives three point three six litres.
So the answer is three point three six litres of carbon dioxide at S T P. The whole trick is moles, then ratio, then molar volume.
एक clean C B S E numerical। दो point two grams propane के complete combustion से बनी carbon dioxide का volume निकालो, S T P पर मापा हुआ।
हमें दिया है: propane का mass दो point two grams, molar mass चौवालीस grams per mole, और S T P पर molar volume बाईस point four litres per mole।
Step one, propane के moles। दो point two बटा चौवालीस देता है zero point zero five moles।
Step two, balanced equation: propane plus पाँच oxygen, तीन carbon dioxide plus चार water देता है।
Step three, mole ratio। एक mole propane तीन moles carbon dioxide देता है, तो zero point zero five moles, zero point one five moles carbon dioxide देता है।
Step four, S T P पर volume। Zero point one five गुणा बाईस point four देता है तीन point three six litres।
तो जवाब है तीन point three six litres carbon dioxide S T P पर। पूरा trick है moles, फिर ratio, फिर molar volume।

board_events.text: [N E E T] Monochloro products of 2-methylbutane
Shortcut: count distinct types of H; each type = one product
Skeleton: $CH_3{-}CH(CH_3){-}CH_2{-}CH_3$
(i) two equivalent methyls on C2 = one type
(ii) the lone tertiary H on C2
(iii) C3 methylene H's; (iv) the C4 methyl
Answer: 4 products. Trap: over-counting to 5 or 6

segments.text: A classic N E E T speed trap. How many distinct monochloro products, ignoring stereoisomers, form when two-methylbutane is chlorinated?
Do not draw every product. Just count the distinct types of hydrogen, because each type of hydrogen gives exactly one monochloro product.
Number the skeleton: a C H three on carbon one, then carbon two carrying the lone hydrogen and a methyl branch, then a C H two on carbon three, then a C H three on carbon four.
Now walk the unique environments. First, the two methyls attached to carbon two are equivalent by symmetry, so together they count as one type.
Second, the single tertiary hydrogen sitting on carbon two, a type all by itself.
Third, the secondary methylene hydrogens on carbon three. And fourth, the methyl hydrogens on carbon four. That is four distinct environments in all.
So the answer is four monochloro products. The trap is over-counting to five or six by forgetting that the two methyls on carbon two are equivalent by symmetry.
एक classic N E E T speed trap। जब two-methylbutane chlorinate होता है, तो कितने distinct monochloro products बनते हैं, stereoisomers को छोड़कर?
हर product मत बनाओ। बस hydrogen के distinct types गिनो, क्योंकि hydrogen का हर type बिल्कुल एक monochloro product देता है।
Skeleton को number करो: carbon one पर एक C H three, फिर carbon two जो lone hydrogen और एक methyl branch carry करता है, फिर carbon three पर एक C H two, फिर carbon four पर एक C H three।
अब unique environments पर चलो। पहला, carbon two से जुड़े दो methyls symmetry से equivalent हैं, तो मिलकर वो एक type गिने जाते हैं।
दूसरा, carbon two पर बैठा अकेला tertiary hydrogen, ख़ुद में एक type।
तीसरा, carbon three पर secondary methylene hydrogens। और चौथा, carbon four पर methyl hydrogens। ये कुल मिलाकर चार distinct environments हैं।
तो जवाब है चार monochloro products। Trap है पाँच या छह तक over-count कर देना, ये भूलकर कि carbon two पर दोनों methyls symmetry से equivalent हैं।

sections.title: Wurtz product and its monochloro count

board_events.text: [J E E Main] Isobutyl bromide, Wurtz, then count products
A is $(CH_3)_2CH{-}CH_2{-}Br$, IUPAC 1-bromo-2-methylpropane
Wurtz couples two such groups through their $CH_2$ ends
Product B: 2,5-dimethylhexane
Distinct H's: 4 equivalent methyls, 2 C2/C5 tertiary H, 2 C3/C4 methylene
Three types $\Rightarrow$ 3 monochloro products

segments.text: A multi-concept J E E Main chain, stitching nomenclature, Wurtz, and product counting into one problem.
Compound A is the branched primary C four H nine bromide, isobutyl bromide, structure two-methylpropane with a bromine on the C H two end. Its I U P A C name is one-bromo-two-methylpropane.
Treat A with sodium in dry ether. Wurtz couples two of these alkyl groups through their C H two ends.
The coupling gives an eight-carbon chain with methyl branches on carbons two and five, plus two sodium bromide.
So product B is two-comma-five-dimethylhexane, a highly symmetric molecule.

Now count its distinct hydrogens: the four equivalent terminal and branch methyls, the two equivalent tertiary hydrogens on carbons two and five, and the two equivalent methylene hydrogens on carbons three and four.
That is three types, so B gives three monochloro products. Symmetry collapses many positions into just three, exactly as in the earlier trap.
एक multi-concept J E E Main chain, जो nomenclature, Wurtz, और product counting को एक problem में जोड़ती है।
Compound A branched primary C four H nine bromide है, isobutyl bromide, structure two-methylpropane जिसके C H two सिरे पर एक bromine है। इसका I U P A C name one-bromo-two-methylpropane है।
A को dry ether में sodium के साथ treat करो। Wurtz इन alkyl groups में से दो को उनके C H two सिरों से couple कर देता है।
Coupling एक आठ-carbon chain देता है जिसमें carbons two और five पर methyl branches हैं, plus दो sodium bromide।
तो product B है two-comma-five-dimethylhexane, एक highly symmetric molecule।
अब इसके distinct hydrogens गिनो: चार equivalent terminal और branch methyls, carbons two और five पर दो equivalent tertiary hydrogens, और carbons three और four पर दो equivalent methylene hydrogens।
ये तीन types हैं, तो B तीन monochloro products देता है। Symmetry बहुत सारी positions को सिर्फ तीन में समेट देती है, ठीक पहले वाले trap की तरह।

board_events.text: [J E E Advanced] 2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane
(i) High m.p.: compact, near-spherical, highly symmetrical molecule
Symmetrical molecules pack efficiently $\Rightarrow$ strong lattice $\Rightarrow$ high m.p.
(ii) All twelve H's are on equivalent methyls: no $2^\circ$ or $3^\circ$ C-H
So chlorination gives ONE product: 1-chloro-2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane
The $3^\circ \gt 2^\circ \gt 1^\circ$ rule is irrelevant when only $1^\circ$ H exist
(iii) Conformations exist in principle, but no separable conformers

segments.text: A J E E Advanced three-parter on two-comma-two-comma-three-comma-three-tetramethylbutane, a solid with a strangely high melting point.
Part one, the high melting point. The molecule is exceptionally compact and symmetrical, almost a sphere.

Highly symmetrical molecules pack efficiently into a crystal lattice, so the lattice is held strongly and a high temperature is needed to melt it. This is the neopentane packing argument taken to an extreme.
Part two. Every hydrogen belongs to a methyl group, and all twelve methyl hydrogens are equivalent by symmetry. There are no secondary or tertiary C H bonds at all.
So free-radical chlorination can give only one monochloro product, one-chloro-two-comma-two-comma-three-comma-three-tetramethylbutane.
And notice the tertiary greater than secondary greater than primary selectivity is completely irrelevant here, because only primary hydrogens exist to be replaced.

Part three. Rotation about the central C C bond turns one tertiary-butyl group against the other, but the three-fold symmetry makes every position essentially equivalent. So the molecule shows conformations in principle, yet no separable conformational isomers.
Two-comma-two-comma-three-comma-three-tetramethylbutane पर एक J E E Advanced तीन-हिस्से वाला सवाल, एक solid जिसका melting point अजीब तरह से ऊँचा है।
Part one, ऊँचा melting point। Molecule असाधारण रूप से compact और symmetrical है, लगभग एक sphere।

Highly symmetrical molecules crystal lattice में efficiently pack होते हैं, इसलिए lattice मज़बूती से बँधा रहता है और उसे पिघलाने के लिए ऊँचा temperature चाहिए। ये neopentane वाला packing argument है, चरम तक ले जाया गया।
Part two। हर hydrogen एक methyl group का है, और सभी बारह methyl hydrogens symmetry से equivalent हैं। कोई secondary या tertiary C H bond है ही नहीं।
तो free-radical chlorination सिर्फ एक monochloro product दे सकता है, one-chloro-two-comma-two-comma-three-comma-three-tetramethylbutane।
और ध्यान दो कि tertiary, secondary से बड़ा, primary से वाली selectivity यहाँ पूरी तरह बेमतलब है, क्योंकि replace होने को सिर्फ primary hydrogens मौजूद हैं।

Part three। Central C C bond के around rotation एक tertiary-butyl group को दूसरे के against घुमाता है, लेकिन three-fold symmetry हर position को असल में equivalent बना देती है। तो molecule principle में conformations दिखाता है, फिर भी कोई separable conformational isomers नहीं।

board_events.text: Four traps that cost marks on alkanes
Trap 1: miscounting monochloro products
Pro-Tip: count distinct H environments; equivalent methyls collapse to one
Trap 2: swapping eclipsed and staggered
Pro-Tip: 'Staggered = Spread = Stable'; eclipsed = $0^\circ$ = max strain
Trap 3: using Wurtz for unsymmetrical alkanes
Trap 4: two orders differ; tag which 'reactivity' the question means

segments.text: Let us close alkanes by locking in the four pitfalls that quietly cost the most marks.
Trap one, miscounting monochloro products. Students list every C H three and C H two position separately and overcount.
Pro tip: count distinct hydrogen environments, using molecular symmetry first, because one environment equals one product. Equivalent methyls collapse to a single type.
Trap two, swapping eclipsed and staggered. Many students wrongly write that eclipsed is most stable.
Pro tip: remember the three S's, staggered equals spread out equals stable. Eclipsed is zero degrees, clouds overlapping, maximum torsional strain.
Trap three, using Wurtz for unsymmetrical alkanes. Coupling two different halides gives three products, not one, so only propose Wurtz for a symmetrical, even-carbon target.

Trap four, confusing the two reactivity orders. The halogen order fluorine to iodine follows electronegativity; the hydrogen order tertiary to primary follows radical stability. Always tag which reactivity the question means before you answer.
चलो alkanes को उन चार pitfalls पक्की करके बंद करें जो चुपचाप सबसे ज़्यादा marks खा जाते हैं।
Trap one, monochloro products को ग़लत गिनना। Students हर C H three और C H two position को अलग-अलग list करके over-count कर देते हैं।
Pro tip: distinct hydrogen environments गिनो, पहले molecular symmetry इस्तेमाल करके, क्योंकि एक environment मतलब एक product। Equivalent methyls एक ही type में सिमट जाते हैं।
Trap two, eclipsed और staggered को आपस में बदल देना। बहुत सारे students ग़लती से लिख देते हैं कि eclipsed सबसे stable है।
Pro tip: तीन S याद रखो, staggered मतलब spread out मतलब stable। Eclipsed zero degrees है, clouds overlap करते हुए, maximum torsional strain।
Trap three, unsymmetrical alkanes के लिए Wurtz इस्तेमाल करना। दो अलग halides couple करने से तीन products मिलते हैं, एक नहीं, इसलिए Wurtz सिर्फ symmetrical, even-carbon target के लिए propose करो।

Trap four, दो reactivity orders को गड्डमड्ड करना। Halogen order, fluorine से iodine, electronegativity follow करता है; hydrogen order, tertiary से primary, radical stability follow करता है। जवाब देने से पहले हमेशा tag करो कि सवाल किस reactivity की बात कर रहा है।

sections.title: The double bond is the whole personality

board_events.text: Alkenes: the train with a folding double-seat
Unsaturated: one $C{=}C$; making it costs two H $\Rightarrow C_nH_{2n}$
Old name 'olefins' (oil-forming)
First stable member: ethene $C_2H_4$
That double bond is the entire personality of the molecule
$\pi$ electrons sit outside the nuclei and are loosely held
One idea runs the sub-topic: alkenes add electrophiles across $C{=}C$

segments.text: <curious>If an alkane is a fully booked train, an alkene is the same train with one pair of adjacent seats left as a folding double-seat, a carbon carbon double bond that springs open the moment a guest wants in.
Alkenes are unsaturated: removing one bond's freedom to make the double bond costs two hydrogens, so the family formula drops to C n H two n.
Their old name is olefins, meaning oil-forming, from the oily product ethene gives with chlorine.
The first stable member is ethene, C two H four. The shorter methene is too short-lived to isolate.
And that double bond is the entire personality of the molecule. Understand it, and almost every reaction of alkenes falls into place.
The reason is that the pi electrons sit outside the line joining the nuclei and are only loosely held, like an exposed pile of cash in a crowded market.
So one idea runs the whole sub-topic: anything hungry for electrons, an electrophile, is drawn straight to that cloud, and alkenes react by adding electrophiles across the double bond.

<curious>अगर alkane एक पूरी तरह booked train है, तो alkene वही train है जिसमें एक जोड़ी adjacent seats folding double-seat की तरह छोड़ दी गई हैं, एक carbon carbon double bond जो मेहमान के आते ही खुल जाती है।
Alkenes unsaturated हैं: double bond बनाने के लिए एक bond की आज़ादी छीनने पर दो hydrogens की क़ीमत लगती है, इसलिए family formula C n H two n हो जाता है।
इनका पुराना नाम olefins है, यानी oil-forming, ethene chlorine के साथ जो oily product देता है उससे।
पहला stable member ethene है, C two H four। इससे छोटा methene इतना short-lived है कि isolate नहीं होता।
और वो double bond ही molecule की पूरी personality है। इसे समझ लो, और alkenes की लगभग हर reaction अपने आप जगह पर बैठ जाती है।
वजह ये है कि pi electrons nuclei को जोड़ने वाली line के बाहर बैठते हैं और सिर्फ ढीले-ढाले पकड़े रहते हैं, जैसे भीड़ भरे बाज़ार में खुला रखा नक़दी का ढेर।
तो एक idea पूरे sub-topic को चलाता है: electrons का भूखा कोई भी, यानी electrophile, सीधे उस cloud की ओर खिंचता है, और alkenes double bond के across electrophiles add करके react करते हैं।

sections.title: Two kinds of glue: sigma and pi

board_events.text: The double bond is built from two different glues
A strong $\sigma$ bond from head-on $sp^2$ overlap: a bolt through the middle
A weaker $\pi$ bond from sideways p-orbital overlap: a rubber band over the top
Compare C-C single = 348 kJ/mol; length $C{=}C$ 134 pm vs $C{-}C$ 154 pm
Poorer lateral overlap makes the $\pi$ bond the weak, exposed part
Adding an electrophile trades the weak $\pi$ for two new stronger $\sigma$ bonds

segments.text: What makes the double bond special is that it is built from two different kinds of glue, and they are not equal.
One is a strong sigma bond, from head-on overlap of s p two orbitals, sturdy like a bolt driven through the middle.
The other is a weaker pi bond, from the sideways overlap of two unhybridised p orbitals, more like a rubber band stretched over the top and bottom.
In numbers, the sigma is about three hundred ninety seven, the pi about two hundred eighty four, so the whole double bond enthalpy is about six hundred eighty one kilojoules per mole.

Compare that with the plain C C single bond at three hundred forty eight kilojoules per mole. The double bond is also shorter: one hundred thirty four picometres against one hundred fifty four for the single bond.
Because the lateral overlap is poorer than head-on, the pi bond is the weak, exposed part of the double bond.
And here is the payoff: when an electrophile adds, that weak pi bond converts into two new, stronger sigma bonds. Reactivity plus a favourable energy trade, all in one idea.
Double bond को ख़ास इस बात से बनाता है कि ये दो अलग तरह के glue से बना है, और वो बराबर नहीं हैं।
एक है strong sigma bond, s p two orbitals के head-on overlap से, मज़बूत जैसे बीच में ठोका हुआ bolt।
दूसरा है weaker pi bond, दो unhybridised p orbitals के sideways overlap से, ज़्यादा जैसे ऊपर-नीचे खिंचा हुआ rubber band।
संख्याओं में, sigma लगभग तीन सौ सत्तानबे है, pi लगभग दो सौ चौरासी, तो पूरी double bond की enthalpy लगभग छह सौ इक्यासी kilojoules per mole है।
इसकी तुलना plain C C single bond से करो, तीन सौ अड़तालीस kilojoules per mole। Double bond छोटा भी है: एक सौ चौंतीस picometres, single bond के एक सौ चौवन के मुक़ाबले।
क्योंकि lateral overlap head-on से कमज़ोर है, pi bond double bond का weak, exposed हिस्सा है।
और यहाँ payoff है: जब कोई electrophile add होता है, वो weak pi bond दो नए, ज़्यादा strong sigma bonds में बदल जाता है। Reactivity plus एक फ़ायदेमंद energy trade, सब एक idea में।

board_events.text: cis = bond dipoles add (more polar); trans = often cancel (zero net dipole)
cis-but-2-ene dipole $\approx 0.33$ D; trans essentially non-polar
Gate: cis-trans needs two DIFFERENT groups on each doubly-bonded carbon

segments.text: Here is a beautiful consequence of that pi bond: picture the double bond as a flat, rigid plank, not a swivelling rod.
Unlike the single bond of ethane, which spins freely, the pi bond locks rotation. To rotate, you would have to snap the rubber band.
So if each end-carbon carries two different groups, those groups are frozen either on the same side, cis, or on opposite sides, trans.
These are geometrical isomers, same connectivity but different fixed shapes in space. In cis-but-two-ene both methyls sit on the same side; in trans they sit on opposite corners.
The cis form is usually slightly polar, because its bond dipoles add up. The symmetric trans form often has zero net dipole.
That is why cis-but-two-ene has a dipole moment of about zero point three three debye, while trans-but-two-ene is essentially non-polar.
Keep the gate on a sticky note: geometrical isomerism appears only when each doubly-bonded carbon bears two different substituents. If either carbon repeats a group, there is no cis-trans pair.
उस pi bond का एक ख़ूबसूरत नतीजा: double bond को एक flat, rigid plank की तरह सोचो, न कि घूमने वाली rod।
Ethane के single bond की तरह नहीं, जो freely घूमता है, pi bond rotation को lock कर देता है। घुमाने के लिए, आपको rubber band तोड़नी पड़ेगी।
तो अगर हर end-carbon दो अलग groups carry करता है, वो groups या तो एक ही तरफ़ freeze हो जाते हैं, cis, या उल्टी तरफ़, trans।
ये geometrical isomers हैं, connectivity वही लेकिन space में fixed shapes अलग। cis-but-two-ene में दोनों methyls एक ही तरफ़ बैठते हैं; trans में वो उल्टे कोनों पर।
cis form आमतौर पर थोड़ा polar होता है, क्योंकि उसके bond dipoles जुड़ जाते हैं। Symmetric trans form का अक्सर net dipole zero होता है।
इसीलिए cis-but-two-ene का dipole moment लगभग zero point three three debye है, जबकि trans-but-two-ene असल में non-polar है।
Gate को sticky note पर रखो: geometrical isomerism सिर्फ तब आता है जब हर doubly-bonded carbon पर दो अलग substituents हों। अगर किसी भी carbon पर कोई group दोहराया गया, तो कोई cis-trans जोड़ी नहीं।

board_events.text: Your alkene fact-sheet
Lengths: $C{=}C = 134$ pm vs $C{-}C = 154$ pm
cis = same side (more polar); trans = opposite (less polar, higher m.p.)
Markovnikov: the negative part adds to the C with FEWER hydrogens
HX reactivity toward alkenes: $HI \gt HBr \gt HCl$
Tests: $Br_2/CCl_4$ decolourised; Baeyer's $KMnO_4$ decolourised

segments.text: Let us pin the alkene facts you must reproduce on demand.
The general formula is C n H two n for one double bond in an acyclic chain, with ethene the first stable member.
Bond enthalpies: sigma three hundred ninety seven plus pi two hundred eighty four give the double bond about six hundred eighty one, against three hundred forty eight for the single bond.
Bond lengths: the double bond is one hundred thirty four picometres, shorter than the single bond at one hundred fifty four.
cis means identical groups on the same side, usually more polar; trans means opposite sides, usually less polar and, for solids, higher melting point.
Markovnikov's rule: the negative part of an unsymmetrical reagent adds to the doubly-bonded carbon that bears the fewer hydrogens, because that routes through the more stable carbocation.
The reactivity of hydrogen halides toward alkenes runs H I greater than H B r greater than H C l, since the weaker H X bond reacts faster.
Two tests for unsaturation: orange bromine in carbon tetrachloride is decolourised, and purple Baeyer's reagent, cold dilute potassium permanganate, is decolourised.
चलो वो alkene facts pin करें जो आपको demand पर reproduce करने आने चाहिए।
General formula एक acyclic chain में एक double bond के लिए C n H two n है, ethene पहला stable member।
Bond enthalpies: sigma तीन सौ सत्तानबे plus pi दो सौ चौरासी मिलकर double bond को लगभग छह सौ इक्यासी देते हैं, single bond के तीन सौ अड़तालीस के मुक़ाबले।
Bond lengths: double bond एक सौ चौंतीस picometres है, single bond के एक सौ चौवन से छोटा।
cis मतलब एक जैसे groups एक ही तरफ़, आमतौर पर ज़्यादा polar; trans मतलब उल्टी तरफ़, आमतौर पर कम polar और, solids के लिए, ऊँचा melting point।
Markovnikov का rule: unsymmetrical reagent का negative हिस्सा उस doubly-bonded carbon पर add होता है जिस पर कम hydrogens हों, क्योंकि वो ज़्यादा stable carbocation से होकर जाता है।
Alkenes की ओर hydrogen halides की reactivity चलती है H I, H B r से बड़ा, H B r, H C l से बड़ा, क्योंकि weaker H X bond तेज़ react करता है।
Unsaturation के दो tests: carbon tetrachloride में orange bromine decolourise हो जाता है, और purple Baeyer's reagent, cold dilute potassium permanganate, decolourise हो जाता है।
