board_events.text: The two perpendicular p orbitals overlap sideways to form the $\pi$ bond
Lateral overlap is poorer, so the $\pi$ bond is weaker (~284 vs 397)
It is this weaker, exposed $\pi$ cloud that the whole reactivity hangs on

segments.text: Let us look under the hood. Each doubly-bonded carbon is s p two hybridised.
Three s p two orbitals lie in a plane at one hundred twenty degrees, forming the two C H bonds and the carbon carbon sigma bond.
The leftover, unhybridised two p orbital stands perpendicular to that plane, pointing above and below.
So the picture is a flat sigma framework in the plane, with a pi cloud sitting above and below it, exactly where reagents can reach.
The two perpendicular p orbitals overlap sideways to form the pi bond above and below the carbon carbon axis.
Because this lateral overlap is poorer than head-on, the pi bond, about two hundred eighty four, is weaker than the sigma, about three hundred ninety seven.
And it is precisely this weaker, exposed pi cloud that the entire reactivity of alkenes hangs on. Everything electrophilic starts here.
चलो hood के नीचे देखें। हर doubly-bonded carbon s p two hybridised है।
तीन s p two orbitals एक plane में एक सौ बीस degrees पर लेटे होते हैं, दो C H bonds और carbon carbon sigma bond बनाते हुए।
बचा हुआ, unhybridised two p orbital उस plane के perpendicular खड़ा रहता है, ऊपर और नीचे की ओर।
तो तस्वीर है plane में एक flat sigma framework, जिसके ऊपर और नीचे एक pi cloud बैठा है, ठीक वहाँ जहाँ reagents पहुँच सकें।
दोनों perpendicular p orbitals sideways overlap करके carbon carbon axis के ऊपर-नीचे pi bond बनाते हैं।
क्योंकि ये lateral overlap head-on से कमज़ोर है, pi bond, लगभग दो सौ चौरासी, sigma, लगभग तीन सौ सत्तानबे, से weaker है।
और ठीक यही weaker, exposed pi cloud है जिस पर alkenes की पूरी reactivity टिकी है। हर electrophilic चीज़ यहीं से शुरू होती है।

board_events.text: IUPAC naming in three moves
(i) pick the longest chain that contains the double bond
(ii) number from the end nearer $C{=}C$ so it gets the lowest locant
(iii) replace -ane with -ene and cite the position
$CH_3CH_2CH{=}CH_2$ is but-1-ene; $CH_3CH{=}CHCH_3$ is but-2-ene
Two or more $C{=}C$ $\Rightarrow$ -diene, -triene (parent kept): buta-1,3-diene
Isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene) is the monomer of natural rubber

segments.text: Naming an alkene takes just three moves, and it is worth doing them in order every time.
First, pick the longest carbon chain that actually contains the double bond, not just the longest chain overall.
Second, number the chain from the end nearer the double bond, so the double bond gets the lowest possible locant.
Third, replace the a n e of the parent alkane with e n e, and cite the position of the double bond.
So the compound C H three C H two C H double bond C H two is but-one-ene, and C H three C H double bond C H C H three is but-two-ene.
When a chain carries more than one double bond, the suffix becomes diene or triene with the parent name kept intact, as in buta-one-three-diene.
One conjugated diene worth naming is isoprene, the monomer of natural rubber, and such conjugated dienes are the bridge to the polymerisation chemistry ahead.
Alkene को name करने में सिर्फ तीन moves लगते हैं, और हर बार उन्हें क्रम से करना फ़ायदेमंद है।
पहला, सबसे लंबी carbon chain चुनो जिसमें असल में double bond हो, सिर्फ overall सबसे लंबी chain नहीं।
दूसरा, chain को उस सिरे से number करो जो double bond के पास हो, ताकि double bond को सबसे कम possible locant मिले।
तीसरा, parent alkane के a n e को e n e से replace करो, और double bond की position बताओ।
तो compound C H three C H two C H double bond C H two, but-one-ene है, और C H three C H double bond C H C H three, but-two-ene है।
जब एक chain में एक से ज़्यादा double bond हों, suffix diene या triene बन जाता है और parent नाम बरक़रार रहता है, जैसे buta-one-three-diene।
एक conjugated diene जिसका नाम लेना ज़रूरी है वो isoprene है, natural rubber का monomer, और ऐसे conjugated dienes आगे आने वाली polymerisation chemistry का bridge हैं।

board_events.text: Physically, alkenes resemble alkanes
Like alkanes: essentially non-polar, held by weak van der Waals forces
First three members gases; next ~fourteen liquids; higher members solids
Insoluble in water; soluble in non-polar solvents (benzene, petroleum ether)
Boiling point rises ~20-30 K per added $-CH_2-$
Branching lowers the surface area for van der Waals contact
A straight-chain alkene boils higher than its branched isomer

segments.text: Physically, alkenes closely resemble alkanes. The differences are mostly in polarity and in the appearance of geometrical isomerism.
Like alkanes, they are essentially non-polar molecules held together only by weak van der Waals forces, so their trends echo the alkanes closely.
The first three members are gases, the next roughly fourteen are liquids, and the higher members are solids.
They are essentially insoluble in water but dissolve well in non-polar solvents such as benzene or petroleum ether.
Boiling point rises steadily, roughly twenty to thirty kelvin for every added C H two unit, just as with alkanes.
And branching lowers the surface area available for van der Waals contact, which drags the boiling point back down.
So the rule carries over from alkanes: a straight-chain alkene boils higher than its branched isomer of the same formula.
Physically, alkenes alkanes से काफ़ी मिलते-जुलते हैं। फ़र्क़ ज़्यादातर polarity में और geometrical isomerism के आने में है।
Alkanes की तरह, ये असल में non-polar molecules हैं जो सिर्फ weak van der Waals forces से जुड़े रहते हैं, इसलिए इनके trends alkanes से काफ़ी मिलते हैं।
पहले तीन members gases हैं, अगले लगभग चौदह liquids हैं, और higher members solids हैं।
ये असल में पानी में insoluble हैं लेकिन non-polar solvents में अच्छे से घुल जाते हैं, जैसे benzene या petroleum ether।
Boiling point steadily बढ़ता है, हर जुड़े C H two unit के लिए लगभग बीस से तीस kelvin, ठीक alkanes की तरह।
और branching van der Waals contact के लिए उपलब्ध surface area कम कर देती है, जो boiling point को वापस नीचे खींचती है।
तो rule alkanes से आगे चलता है: एक straight-chain alkene अपने same formula वाले branched isomer से ऊँचे तापमान पर boil होता है।

sections.title: Making alkenes I: from alkynes (geometry control)

board_events.text: Partial reduction of alkynes sets the geometry
Lindlar's catalyst (poisoned Pd) stops at the alkene and gives cis
Sodium in liquid ammonia gives the trans isomer
Lindlar's Pd is poisoned so it stops at the alkene instead of pushing to the alkane
Lindlar $\Rightarrow$ syn addition $\Rightarrow$ cis; Na/$NH_3$ $\Rightarrow$ trans
The choice of reducing system SETS the geometry: a favourite exam hook

segments.text: <curious>The first route to an alkene is a clever one, because it lets you choose the geometry: partial reduction of an alkyne.
Partial hydrogenation over Lindlar's catalyst, palladised charcoal poisoned with sulphur or quinoline, stops cleanly at the alkene and delivers the cis isomer.
Reduction with sodium in liquid ammonia, on the other hand, gives the trans isomer of the same alkene.
The poison on Lindlar's palladium is the whole point: it deliberately weakens the catalyst so the reduction stops at the alkene instead of running all the way to the alkane.
For example, but-two-yne with sodium in liquid ammonia gives trans-but-two-ene.
So remember the pairing: Lindlar gives syn addition of hydrogen and therefore cis, while sodium in ammonia gives trans.
The choice of reducing system sets the geometry, and that is a favourite exam hook. It is also why preparation from alkynes appears in both this sub-topic and the alkyne one.
<curious>Alkene का पहला route चतुर है, क्योंकि ये आपको geometry चुनने देता है: एक alkyne का partial reduction।
Lindlar's catalyst पर partial hydrogenation, sulphur या quinoline से poisoned palladised charcoal, साफ़ तौर पर alkene पर रुक जाता है और cis isomer देता है।
दूसरी ओर, liquid ammonia में sodium से reduction उसी alkene का trans isomer देता है।
Lindlar's palladium पर लगा poison ही असली बात है: ये जानबूझकर catalyst को कमज़ोर करता है ताकि reduction alkane तक जाने के बजाय alkene पर रुक जाए।
मिसाल के तौर पर, but-two-yne liquid ammonia में sodium के साथ trans-but-two-ene देता है।
तो जोड़ी याद रखो: Lindlar hydrogen का syn addition और इसलिए cis देता है, जबकि ammonia में sodium trans देता है।
Reducing system का चुनाव geometry तय करता है, और ये एक favourite exam hook है। यही वजह है कि alkynes से preparation इस sub-topic और alkyne वाले, दोनों में आता है।

board_events.text: Three more routes, all eliminations
(b) Dehydrohalogenation: R-X + alcoholic KOH removes one HX
H leaves the $\beta$-carbon $\Rightarrow \beta$-elimination; rates $I \gt Br \gt Cl$, $3^\circ \gt 2^\circ \gt 1^\circ$
(c) Dehalogenation: a vicinal dihalide + Zn loses $ZnX_2$
(d) Dehydration: alcohol + conc. $H_2SO_4$ eliminates water
All four routes remove atoms to unveil a $C{=}C$

segments.text: The remaining three routes are all eliminations: you strip atoms off a saturated molecule to unveil a double bond.
Route b is dehydrohalogenation. Heating an alkyl halide with alcoholic potassium hydroxide removes one molecule of H X.

The hydrogen leaves from the beta carbon, the one next to the halogen, so this is a beta elimination. Rates run iodide greater than bromide greater than chloride, and tertiary greater than secondary greater than primary.
Route c is dehalogenation. A dihalide with halogens on adjacent carbons loses zinc halide when treated with zinc dust, regenerating the double bond.
So one-two-dibromoethane plus zinc gives ethene plus zinc bromide.
Route d is acidic dehydration. Heating an alcohol with concentrated sulphuric acid eliminates water; the hydroxyl pulls a hydrogen off the beta carbon, so this too is a beta elimination.
Step back and the pattern is clear: every route to an alkene either partly reduces an alkyne or eliminates atoms to unveil the double bond.
बाक़ी तीन routes सब eliminations हैं: आप एक saturated molecule से atoms छीलकर double bond को उजागर करते हैं।
Route b dehydrohalogenation है। एक alkyl halide को alcoholic potassium hydroxide के साथ गरम करने से H X का एक molecule निकल जाता है।

Hydrogen beta carbon से जाता है, वो जो halogen के बगल वाला है, तो ये beta elimination है। Rates चलती हैं iodide, bromide से बड़ा, bromide, chloride से, और tertiary, secondary से, secondary, primary से।
Route c dehalogenation है। adjacent carbons पर halogens वाला एक dihalide zinc dust के साथ treat करने पर zinc halide खो देता है, double bond वापस बना देता है।
तो one-two-dibromoethane plus zinc, ethene plus zinc bromide देता है।
Route d acidic dehydration है। एक alcohol को concentrated sulphuric acid के साथ गरम करने से पानी निकल जाता है; hydroxyl beta carbon से एक hydrogen खींचता है, तो ये भी एक beta elimination है।
पीछे हटकर देखो तो pattern साफ़ है: alkene का हर route या तो किसी alkyne को partly reduce करता है या atoms eliminate करके double bond उजागर करता है।

board_events.text: The master reaction: electrophiles attack the $\pi$ bond
Addition of $H_2$ over Ni/Pd/Pt $\to$ alkane
Addition of halogens: $Br_2$ or $Cl_2$ $\to$ a vicinal dihalide
Iodine does not add under normal conditions
Decolourising $Br_2/CCl_4$ is the classic test (via a cyclic halonium ion)
Alkenes are electron-rich: every reaction starts with an electrophile hitting the $\pi$ cloud

segments.text: Now the master reaction. Alkenes are electron-rich, so every reaction begins with an electrophile attacking the pi bond.
First, addition of hydrogen over nickel, palladium, or platinum gives the alkane, the very same hydrogenation we met with alkanes.
Second, bromine or chlorine adds to give a vicinal dihalide, with the halogens landing on adjacent carbons.
Ethene plus bromine gives one-two-dibromoethane.
Iodine, on the other hand, does not add across the double bond under normal conditions.
The decolourisation of orange bromine in carbon tetrachloride is the classic test for unsaturation, and mechanistically it goes through a cyclic halonium ion.
Hold the theme steady: because alkenes are electron-rich, every addition starts with an electrophile hitting the pi cloud, and then a nucleophile completes the job.
अब master reaction। Alkenes electron-rich हैं, इसलिए हर reaction एक electrophile के pi bond पर हमला करने से शुरू होती है।
पहला, nickel, palladium, या platinum पर hydrogen का addition alkane देता है, वही hydrogenation जो हमने alkanes के साथ देखी थी।
दूसरा, bromine या chlorine add होकर एक vicinal dihalide देता है, halogens adjacent carbons पर बैठते हुए।
Ethene plus bromine, one-two-dibromoethane देता है।
दूसरी ओर, iodine normal conditions में double bond के across add नहीं होता।
Carbon tetrachloride में orange bromine का decolourise होना unsaturation का classic test है, और mechanism के हिसाब से ये एक cyclic halonium ion से होकर जाता है।
Theme को स्थिर रखो: क्योंकि alkenes electron-rich हैं, हर addition एक electrophile के pi cloud पर टकराने से शुरू होता है, और फिर एक nucleophile काम पूरा करता है।

board_events.text: Adding H-X: which carbon gets what?
The reagent adds through the MORE stable carbocation
Step 1: $\pi$ electrons grab the proton, opening $C{=}C$ into a carbocation
The reaction routes through whichever cation is more stable
Step 2: bromide attacks the cation; the $2^\circ$ beats the $1^\circ$, so 2-bromopropane wins
Markovnikov, restated: the product forms via the most stable accessible carbocation

segments.text: When a hydrogen halide adds to an unsymmetrical alkene, the real question is which carbon gets the hydrogen and which gets the halogen.
The answer is always the same: the reagent adds so that the reaction passes through the more stable carbocation.
With propene and H B r, the major product is two-bromopropane.
Spell out the two steps. In step one, the pi electrons grab the proton, opening the double bond into a carbocation.
The proton can give either a primary or a secondary carbocation, and the reaction routes through whichever one is more stable.
In step two the bromide ion attacks that carbocation. Because the secondary cation is more stable than the primary, the bromide caps that carbon, and two-bromopropane is the major product.
So restate Markovnikov as the useful version: the product forms via the most stable accessible carbocation. That single sentence predicts almost every H X addition.
जब एक hydrogen halide किसी unsymmetrical alkene में add होता है, असली सवाल है कि कौन सा carbon hydrogen पाता है और कौन सा halogen।
जवाब हमेशा एक ही है: reagent इस तरह add होता है कि reaction ज़्यादा stable carbocation से होकर गुज़रे।
Propene और H B r के साथ, major product two-bromopropane है।
दोनों steps खोलकर देखो। Step one में, pi electrons proton को पकड़ते हैं, double bond को खोलकर carbocation बना देते हैं।
Proton या तो primary या secondary carbocation दे सकता है, और reaction उसी में से होकर जाती है जो ज़्यादा stable हो।
Step two में bromide ion उस carbocation पर हमला करता है। क्योंकि secondary cation primary से ज़्यादा stable है, bromide उसी carbon को cap करता है, और two-bromopropane major product है।
तो Markovnikov को useful version में दोहराओ: product सबसे ज़्यादा stable accessible carbocation से होकर बनता है। वो एक sentence लगभग हर H X addition predict कर देता है।

board_events.text: Peroxide flips the orientation, but only for HBr
With peroxide, HBr adds to propene against Markovnikov $\to$ 1-bromopropane
It runs by a free-radical chain (initiation, propagation, termination)
The Br radical adds to give the more stable $2^\circ$ carbon radical
HBr-only: H-Cl (~431) too strong; H-I (~297) too weak, I radicals recombine
Memory hook: 'Br Breaks the Rule'
HCl and HI always follow plain Markovnikov, peroxide or not

segments.text: <excited>Now a twist that examiners love. Add an organic peroxide, and H B r adds to propene against Markovnikov.
Instead of two-bromopropane, you get one-bromopropane, with the bromine on the terminal carbon.
It runs by a free-radical chain, the same initiation, propagation, termination framework as alkane halogenation.
The bromine radical adds so as to give the more stable secondary carbon radical, which places the bromine on the terminal carbon.

Crucially, the effect is H B r only. The H C l bond, about four hundred thirty one, is too strong for the peroxide radical to cleave, and the H I bond, about two hundred ninety seven, is so weak that iodine radicals simply recombine instead of adding.
So the memory hook is B r breaks the rule. Only H B r reverses under peroxide.
H C l and H I always follow plain Markovnikov, whether or not a peroxide is present.
<excited>अब एक twist जो examiners को बहुत पसंद है। एक organic peroxide डालो, और H B r propene में Markovnikov के ख़िलाफ़ add होता है।
Two-bromopropane की जगह, आपको one-bromopropane मिलता है, bromine terminal carbon पर।
ये एक free-radical chain से चलता है, वही initiation, propagation, termination framework जो alkane halogenation में था।
Bromine radical इस तरह add होता है कि ज़्यादा stable secondary carbon radical बने, जो bromine को terminal carbon पर रख देता है।

बहुत ज़रूरी, ये effect सिर्फ H B r के लिए है। H C l bond, लगभग चार सौ इकत्तीस, इतना strong है कि peroxide radical उसे तोड़ नहीं सकता, और H I bond, लगभग दो सौ सत्तानबे, इतना weak है कि iodine radicals add होने के बजाय बस फिर से जुड़ जाते हैं।
तो memory hook है B r breaks the rule। सिर्फ H B r peroxide में उल्टा होता है।
H C l और H I हमेशा plain Markovnikov follow करते हैं, चाहे peroxide मौजूद हो या नहीं।

board_events.text: Two more Markovnikov additions
Cold conc. $H_2SO_4$ adds (Markovnikov) $\to$ an alkyl hydrogen sulphate
Water adds with a little $H_2SO_4$ (Markovnikov) $\to$ an alcohol
The proton adds first to give the more stable cation, then the nucleophile caps it
Same two-step, carbocation-controlled logic as HX
Both route through the more stable carbocation, exactly like HX
Water addition is a standard lab route from alkene to alcohol

segments.text: Two more additions round out the H X family, and both follow Markovnikov through the same carbocation logic.
Cold concentrated sulphuric acid adds across the double bond, Markovnikov fashion, to give an alkyl hydrogen sulphate.
Water adds in the presence of a little sulphuric acid, again Markovnikov, to give an alcohol.
The mechanism is familiar: the proton adds first to give the more stable cation, and then the nucleophile, hydrogen sulphate or water, caps that carbon.
So it is the same two-step, carbocation-controlled logic as ordinary H X addition, just with a different nucleophile.
And because both route through the more stable carbocation, you can predict the product with the very same Markovnikov reasoning.
Practically, this water addition is a standard laboratory route from an alkene to an alcohol.
दो और additions H X family को पूरा करते हैं, और दोनों उसी carbocation logic से Markovnikov follow करते हैं।
Cold concentrated sulphuric acid double bond के across add होता है, Markovnikov तरीक़े से, और एक alkyl hydrogen sulphate देता है।
थोड़े sulphuric acid की मौजूदगी में पानी add होता है, फिर Markovnikov, और एक alcohol देता है।
Mechanism जाना-पहचाना है: proton पहले add होकर ज़्यादा stable cation देता है, और फिर nucleophile, hydrogen sulphate या पानी, उस carbon को cap करता है।
तो ये वही two-step, carbocation-controlled logic है जो ordinary H X addition की है, बस nucleophile अलग है।
और क्योंकि दोनों ज़्यादा stable carbocation से होकर जाते हैं, आप product को उसी Markovnikov reasoning से predict कर सकते हो।
Practically, ये water addition एक alkene से alcohol तक पहुँचने का standard laboratory route है।

board_events.text: Oxidation comes in two strengths
Cold dilute alkaline $KMnO_4$ (Baeyer's) $\to$ a vicinal glycol, decolourising purple
That decolourisation is a second unsaturation test
Hot acidic $KMnO_4$ or $K_2Cr_2O_7$ CLEAVES the double bond
A $=CH$ carbon becomes $-COOH$; a carbon with two alkyls becomes a ketone

segments.text: Oxidation of an alkene comes in two strengths, mild and forcing, and they do very different things.
Cold, dilute, alkaline potassium permanganate, that is Baeyer's reagent, oxidises the alkene to a vicinal glycol, a diol on adjacent carbons, and the purple colour discharges.
So ethene is converted to ethane-one-two-diol.
That decolourisation is a second test for unsaturation, alongside the bromine water test.
Under more forcing conditions, hot acidic potassium permanganate or potassium dichromate, the double bond is not just hydroxylated but cleaved into ketones and acids.
For instance, but-two-ene is cleaved to two molecules of ethanoic acid.
The rule for cleavage: a doubly-bonded C H carbon ends up as a carboxylic acid, while a carbon carrying two alkyl groups becomes a ketone. Read backwards, that locates the double bond.
एक alkene का oxidation दो strengths में आता है, mild और forcing, और वो बहुत अलग काम करते हैं।
Cold, dilute, alkaline potassium permanganate, यानी Baeyer's reagent, alkene को एक vicinal glycol में oxidise करता है, adjacent carbons पर एक diol, और purple रंग ग़ायब हो जाता है।
तो ethene, ethane-one-two-diol में बदल जाता है।
वो decolourisation unsaturation का दूसरा test है, bromine water test के साथ-साथ।
ज़्यादा forcing conditions में, hot acidic potassium permanganate या potassium dichromate से, double bond सिर्फ hydroxylate नहीं होता बल्कि ketones और acids में cleave हो जाता है।
मिसाल के तौर पर, but-two-ene दो molecules ethanoic acid में cleave हो जाता है।
Cleavage का rule: एक doubly-bonded C H carbon carboxylic acid बन जाता है, जबकि दो alkyl groups वाला carbon ketone बन जाता है। उल्टा पढ़ो, तो वो double bond ढूँढ देता है।

Ozone adds to $C{=}C$ to form an ozonide
$Zn{-}H_2O$ then cleaves the ozonide into two carbonyl fragments

board_events.text: Read the products backwards to locate the original double bond
A carbon with two alkyls $\to$ ketone; a carbon with an H $\to$ aldehyde
Polymerisation: many ethene units add $\to$ polythene (addition polymerisation)

segments.text: <curious>Ozonolysis is the sharpest structure-finding tool in the sub-topic: cut the double bond cleanly and read the pieces backwards.
First, ozone adds to the double bond to form a five-membered ozonide.
Then zinc and water cleave that ozonide into two carbonyl fragments.
Here is the scheme: alkene plus ozone gives the ozonide, then zinc and water split it into two carbonyl compounds.
The trick is to read the products backwards: join the two carbonyl carbons and you have located the original double bond.
The reading rule: a double-bond carbon that carried two alkyl groups gives a ketone, and one that carried a hydrogen gives an aldehyde.
Finally, polymerisation. Many ethene molecules simply add to one another with no small molecule lost, giving polythene. Because nothing is lost, it is called addition polymerisation.
<curious>Ozonolysis इस sub-topic का सबसे तेज़ structure-finding tool है: double bond को साफ़ काटो और टुकड़ों को उल्टा पढ़ो।
पहले, ozone double bond में add होकर एक five-membered ozonide बनाता है।
फिर zinc और पानी उस ozonide को दो carbonyl fragments में cleave कर देते हैं।
ये रहा scheme: alkene plus ozone ozonide देता है, फिर zinc और पानी उसे दो carbonyl compounds में तोड़ देते हैं।
Trick है products को उल्टा पढ़ना: दोनों carbonyl carbons को जोड़ो और आपने original double bond ढूँढ लिया।
पढ़ने का rule: एक double-bond carbon जिस पर दो alkyl groups थे वो ketone देता है, और जिस पर एक hydrogen था वो aldehyde देता है।
आख़िर में, polymerisation। बहुत सारे ethene molecules बिना कोई छोटा molecule खोए एक-दूसरे में add होकर polythene बनाते हैं। क्योंकि कुछ नहीं खोता, इसे addition polymerisation कहते हैं।

sections.title: but-1-ene + HBr, with and without peroxide

board_events.text: [C B S E] but-1-ene + HBr, with and without peroxide
But-1-ene, $CH_3CH_2CH{=}CH_2$, is an unsymmetrical alkene
(i) Without peroxide (Markovnikov): H to terminal $CH_2$, Br to $C_2$
Product: 2-bromobutane (Markovnikov rule)
(ii) With peroxide (Kharasch): Br adds to the terminal carbon
Product: 1-bromobutane (peroxide / anti-Markovnikov effect)

segments.text: A clean C B S E question. Write the products when but-one-ene reacts with H B r, first without peroxide and then with peroxide.
But-one-ene is C H three C H two C H double bond C H two, an unsymmetrical alkene, so orientation matters.
Without peroxide, Markovnikov applies. The proton adds to the terminal C H two, which has more hydrogens, and bromine goes to carbon two, through the more stable secondary carbocation.
So the product is C H three C H two C H bromine C H three.
That is two-bromobutane, formed by the Markovnikov rule.
With peroxide, the Kharasch effect flips the orientation, so bromine adds to the terminal carbon instead.
So the second product is one-bromobutane, by the peroxide or anti-Markovnikov effect. Same reagent, opposite regiochemistry.
एक clean C B S E सवाल। लिखो कि जब but-one-ene, H B r के साथ react करता है तो products क्या हैं, पहले बिना peroxide और फिर peroxide के साथ।
But-one-ene, C H three C H two C H double bond C H two है, एक unsymmetrical alkene, इसलिए orientation मायने रखता है।
बिना peroxide, Markovnikov लागू होता है। Proton terminal C H two पर add होता है, जिस पर ज़्यादा hydrogens हैं, और bromine carbon two पर जाता है, ज़्यादा stable secondary carbocation से होकर।
तो product है C H three C H two C H bromine C H three।
वो two-bromobutane है, Markovnikov rule से बना।
Peroxide के साथ, Kharasch effect orientation पलट देता है, तो bromine इसके बजाय terminal carbon पर add होता है।
तो दूसरा product one-bromobutane है, peroxide या anti-Markovnikov effect से। वही reagent, उल्टी regiochemistry।

board_events.text: [N E E T] Which shows cis-trans isomerism?
The one-line gate: each doubly-bonded carbon must carry two DIFFERENT groups
(A) 2-methylbut-2-ene $(CH_3)_2C{=}CHCH_3$: left carbon has two methyls $\Rightarrow$ fails
(B) pent-2-ene $CH_3CH{=}CHCH_2CH_3$: each carbon has H and an alkyl $\Rightarrow$ passes
(C) 2-methylprop-1-ene $(CH_3)_2C{=}CH_2$: both carbons carry identical pairs $\Rightarrow$ fails
Answer: only (B) pent-2-ene
Trap: assuming (A) qualifies just because it is a branched 2-ene

segments.text: A classic N E E T speed trap. Of three candidates, which one shows geometrical, cis-trans, isomerism?
Do not draw anything. Apply the one-line gate: each carbon of the double bond must carry two different groups.
Candidate A, two-methylbut-two-ene: the left carbon of the double bond carries two identical methyls, so it fails the gate.
Candidate B, pent-two-ene: the left carbon has a hydrogen and a methyl, the right carbon a hydrogen and an ethyl, both pairs different, so it passes.
Candidate C, two-methylprop-one-ene: both carbons carry identical pairs, so it fails.
So the answer is only B, pent-two-ene.
The trap is seeing a two-ene with a methyl branch in A and assuming it qualifies, forgetting to check that one carbon already carries two identical groups.
एक classic N E E T speed trap। तीन candidates में से, कौन सा geometrical, cis-trans, isomerism दिखाता है?
कुछ मत बनाओ। One-line gate लगाओ: double bond के हर carbon पर दो अलग groups होने चाहिए।
Candidate A, two-methylbut-two-ene: double bond के left carbon पर दो एक जैसे methyls हैं, तो ये gate में fail हो जाता है।
Candidate B, pent-two-ene: left carbon पर एक hydrogen और एक methyl, right carbon पर एक hydrogen और एक ethyl, दोनों जोड़ियाँ अलग, तो ये pass हो जाता है।
Candidate C, two-methylprop-one-ene: दोनों carbons पर एक जैसी जोड़ियाँ हैं, तो ये fail हो जाता है।
तो जवाब है सिर्फ B, pent-two-ene।
Trap है A में एक methyl branch वाला two-ene देखकर मान लेना कि वो qualify करता है, ये check करना भूलकर कि एक carbon पर पहले से दो एक जैसे groups हैं।

board_events.text: [J E E Main] $C_5H_{10}$: ozonolysis gives propanal + ethanal
Reverse the ozonolysis: stitch the two carbonyl carbons into a $C{=}C$
Propanal $CH_3CH_2CHO$ + ethanal $CH_3CHO$: join the carbonyl carbons
That is $C_5H_{10}$: A is pent-2-ene
(ii) With HBr/peroxide the internal alkene gives mainly 3-bromopentane
Peroxide reverses orientation only with a clear $1^\circ$-vs-$2^\circ$ choice

segments.text: A multi-concept J E E Main problem. An alkene A, formula C five H ten, gives propanal and ethanal on reductive ozonolysis. Find A, then react it with H B r and peroxide.
To find A, reverse the ozonolysis: stitch the two carbonyl carbons back together with a double bond.
Propanal is C H three C H two C H O and ethanal is C H three C H O. Join their carbonyl carbons.
That gives C H three C H two C H double bond C H C H three.
That is C five H ten, so A is pent-two-ene.

Now part two. Pent-two-ene is symmetric in substitution, both carbons carry alkyl groups. With peroxide the radical route still favours the more stable secondary radical, giving predominantly three-bromopentane, with two-bromopentane minor.
The teaching point: the peroxide effect reverses orientation only when there is a clear primary versus secondary choice. For an internal alkene, the regiochemical effect is muted.
एक multi-concept J E E Main problem। एक alkene A, formula C five H ten, reductive ozonolysis पर propanal और ethanal देता है। A ढूँढो, फिर उसे H B r और peroxide के साथ react करो।
A ढूँढने के लिए, ozonolysis को उल्टा करो: दोनों carbonyl carbons को double bond से वापस जोड़ दो।
Propanal, C H three C H two C H O है और ethanal, C H three C H O है। इनके carbonyl carbons को जोड़ो।
इससे मिलता है C H three C H two C H double bond C H C H three।
वो C five H ten है, तो A pent-two-ene है।

अब part two। Pent-two-ene substitution में symmetric है, दोनों carbons पर alkyl groups हैं। Peroxide के साथ radical route अब भी ज़्यादा stable secondary radical को favour करता है, जिससे मुख्यतः three-bromopentane बनता है, two-bromopentane minor।
Teaching point: peroxide effect orientation सिर्फ तब पलटता है जब एक साफ़ primary बनाम secondary choice हो। एक internal alkene के लिए, regiochemical effect दब जाता है।

board_events.text: [J E E Advanced] 3-methylbut-1-ene + HCl
Major product is 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, not 2-chloro-3-methylbutane
Protonation of the terminal $CH_2$ gives a $2^\circ$ carbocation at $C_2$
The $3^\circ$ cation is markedly more stable, so chloride caps it
Result: 2-chloro-2-methylbutane as the major product
Driving force: trade a $2^\circ$ cation for a more stable $3^\circ$: the real Markovnikov rule

segments.text: A J E E Advanced favourite on carbocation rearrangement. When three-methylbut-one-ene meets H C l, the major product is not the naive Markovnikov one.
The major product is two-chloro-two-methylbutane, not the simple Markovnikov two-chloro-three-methylbutane. Something rearranges.
Protonation of the terminal C H two gives, by Markovnikov, a secondary carbocation at carbon two.
But the adjacent carbon, carbon three, carries a hydrogen and two methyls. A one-two hydride shift moves that hydrogen across, turning the secondary cation into a tertiary one.
The tertiary cation is markedly more stable, thanks to greater hyperconjugation and induction, so chloride caps it.
The result is two-chloro-two-methylbutane as the major product.
The driving force is trading a less stable secondary cation for a more stable tertiary one. This is exactly why Markovnikov must be stated as the product via the most stable accessible carbocation.
Carbocation rearrangement पर एक J E E Advanced favourite। जब three-methylbut-one-ene, H C l से मिलता है, major product naive Markovnikov वाला नहीं होता।
Major product two-chloro-two-methylbutane है, simple Markovnikov two-chloro-three-methylbutane नहीं। कुछ rearrange होता है।
Terminal C H two का protonation, Markovnikov से, carbon two पर एक secondary carbocation देता है।
लेकिन बगल वाला carbon, carbon three, एक hydrogen और दो methyls carry करता है। एक one-two hydride shift उस hydrogen को खिसका देता है, secondary cation को tertiary में बदलते हुए।
Tertiary cation काफ़ी ज़्यादा stable है, ज़्यादा hyperconjugation और induction की वजह से, तो chloride उसे cap करता है।
नतीजा है two-chloro-two-methylbutane major product के तौर पर।
Driving force है एक कम stable secondary cation को ज़्यादा stable tertiary से बदलना। यही वजह है कि Markovnikov को सबसे stable accessible carbocation से बनने वाला product कहना पड़ता है।

board_events.text: Four traps that cost marks on alkenes
Trap 1: claiming cis-trans without checking substituents
Gate: each doubly-bonded carbon needs two different groups, else no cis-trans pair
Trap 2: applying the peroxide effect to HCl or HI
Trap 3: forgetting carbocation rearrangement
Pro-Tip: after the first cation, ask 'can a 1,2-shift reach a $3^\circ$?'
Trap 4: to rebuild the alkene, join carbonyls; ketone = two alkyls, aldehyde = had an H

segments.text: Let us close alkenes with the four pitfalls that quietly cost the most marks.
Trap one, labelling any internal alkene as cis or trans without checking the substituents.
Pro tip: apply the one-line gate. Each doubly-bonded carbon must carry two different groups. If either carbon repeats a group, there is no cis-trans pair.
Trap two, applying the peroxide effect to H C l or H I. The Kharasch anti-Markovnikov effect is H B r only. Remember, B r breaks the rule.
Trap three, forgetting carbocation rearrangement. The Markovnikov product is wrong whenever a hydride or methyl shift can reach a more stable cation.
Pro tip: after writing the first carbocation, always ask whether a one-two shift can reach a tertiary or more stable cation before you place the nucleophile.

Trap four, mis-assembling ozonolysis products. To rebuild the alkene, join the carbonyl carbons with a double bond. A ketone fragment means that carbon had two alkyl groups; an aldehyde means it had a hydrogen.
चलो alkenes को उन चार pitfalls के साथ बंद करें जो चुपचाप सबसे ज़्यादा marks खा जाते हैं।
Trap one, किसी भी internal alkene को substituents check किए बिना cis या trans कह देना।
Pro tip: one-line gate लगाओ। हर doubly-bonded carbon पर दो अलग groups होने चाहिए। अगर किसी भी carbon पर कोई group दोहराया गया, तो कोई cis-trans जोड़ी नहीं।
Trap two, peroxide effect को H C l या H I पर लगाना। Kharasch anti-Markovnikov effect सिर्फ H B r के लिए है। याद रखो, B r breaks the rule।
Trap three, carbocation rearrangement भूल जाना। Markovnikov product तब ग़लत है जब कोई hydride या methyl shift ज़्यादा stable cation तक पहुँच सके।
Pro tip: पहला carbocation लिखने के बाद, nucleophile रखने से पहले हमेशा पूछो कि क्या कोई one-two shift किसी tertiary या ज़्यादा stable cation तक पहुँच सकता है।

Trap four, ozonolysis products को ग़लत जोड़ना। Alkene दोबारा बनाने के लिए, carbonyl carbons को double bond से जोड़ो। एक ketone fragment का मतलब उस carbon पर दो alkyl groups थे; एक aldehyde का मतलब उस पर एक hydrogen था।

sections.title: Pull the carbons closer, add a third bond

board_events.text: The triple bond: tightest link in the chapter
Losing another pair of H drops the formula to $C_nH_{2n-2}$
Headline member: ethyne, common name acetylene
Burned with oxygen in an oxy-acetylene torch: hot enough to weld steel
Built from one $\sigma$ bond plus TWO weaker $\pi$ bonds
Two $\pi$ clouds wrap the axis in a cylinder of loosely-held electrons
With two $\pi$ bonds to spend, an alkyne can add TWO molecules of a reagent

segments.text: <curious>Take an alkene's double bond, pull the two carbons even closer, and bind them with a third shared pair. Now you have an alkyne, a hydrocarbon with a carbon carbon triple bond.
Losing yet another pair of hydrogens drops the family formula to C n H two n minus two.
The headline member is ethyne, universally known by its common name acetylene.
Burned with oxygen in an oxy-acetylene torch, it gives a flame hot enough to weld steel.
The triple bond is built from one sigma bond, from head-on overlap of s p orbitals, plus two weaker pi bonds from two perpendicular pairs of p orbitals.
Those two pi clouds wrap the bond axis in a cylinder of loosely held electrons, so an alkyne, like an alkene, is an electron-rich target electrophiles love.
But here is the difference: with two pi bonds to spend, an alkyne can add two molecules of a reagent. That double-barrelled reactivity is the whole flavour of the sub-topic.
<curious>एक alkene का double bond लो, दोनों carbons को और पास खींचो, और उन्हें एक तीसरी shared जोड़ी से बाँध दो। अब आपके पास एक alkyne है, एक hydrocarbon जिसमें carbon carbon triple bond है।
एक और जोड़ी hydrogens खोने से family formula C n H two n minus two हो जाता है।
Headline member ethyne है, जिसे सब उसके common name acetylene से जानते हैं।
Oxygen के साथ oxy-acetylene torch में जलाया जाए, तो ये इतनी गरम flame देता है कि steel weld हो जाए।
Triple bond एक sigma bond से बना है, s p orbitals के head-on overlap से, plus दो weaker pi bonds दो perpendicular p orbital जोड़ियों से।
वो दो pi clouds bond axis को loosely held electrons के एक cylinder में लपेट देते हैं, तो एक alkyne, alkene की तरह, एक electron-rich target है जिसे electrophiles पसंद करते हैं।
लेकिन यहाँ फ़र्क़ है: ख़र्च करने को दो pi bonds होने से, एक alkyne किसी reagent के दो molecules add कर सकता है। वो double-barrelled reactivity ही इस sub-topic का पूरा स्वाद है।

board_events.text: Why the terminal hydrogen is acidic
$sp^3$ carbon = one-quarter s; $sp^2$ = one-third; $sp$ = fully half s
An s orbital hugs the nucleus more tightly than a p orbital
So more s-character makes the carbon more electronegative
So in ethyne the C-H hydrogen slips off as $H^+$ more readily
Only a hydrogen on a triply-bonded carbon counts as acidic
More s-character = more acidic terminal H (the most-tested idea here)
So terminal alkynes form metal acetylides; alkenes and alkanes do not

segments.text: Think about it this way: a carbon's personality is set by how much s-character its hybrid orbitals carry.
An s p three carbon is one-quarter s; an s p two carbon is one-third s; and an s p carbon is fully half s.
Because an s orbital hugs the nucleus more tightly than a p orbital, more s-character pulls the shared electrons closer in.
So more s-character makes the carbon more electronegative, and it grips the shared electrons of its C H bond harder.
So in ethyne the C H hydrogen can slip off as a proton far more readily than in ethene or ethane.
And note the fine print already: only a hydrogen sitting directly on a triply-bonded carbon is acidic in this way.
That single idea, more s-character means a more acidic terminal hydrogen, is the most-tested concept in the whole sub-topic.
It is exactly why terminal alkynes react with strong bases to form metal acetylides, releasing hydrogen, while alkenes and alkanes do not.
इसे ऐसे सोचो: एक carbon की personality इससे तय होती है कि उसके hybrid orbitals में कितना s-character है।
एक s p three carbon एक-चौथाई s है; एक s p two carbon एक-तिहाई s है; और एक s p carbon पूरा आधा s है।
क्योंकि एक s orbital nucleus को एक p orbital से ज़्यादा कसकर पकड़ता है, ज़्यादा s-character shared electrons को और पास खींच लेता है।
तो ज़्यादा s-character carbon को ज़्यादा electronegative बनाता है, और वो अपने C H bond के shared electrons को ज़्यादा कसकर पकड़ता है।
तो ethyne में C H hydrogen एक proton की तरह ethene या ethane के मुक़ाबले कहीं ज़्यादा आसानी से निकल जाता है।
और अभी से fine print पर ध्यान दो: सिर्फ वो hydrogen जो सीधे एक triply-bonded carbon पर बैठा हो, इस तरह acidic होता है।
वो एक idea, ज़्यादा s-character मतलब ज़्यादा acidic terminal hydrogen, पूरे sub-topic का सबसे ज़्यादा test होने वाला concept है।
यही वजह है कि terminal alkynes strong bases के साथ react करके metal acetylides बनाते हैं, hydrogen release करते हुए, जबकि alkenes और alkanes नहीं।

board_events.text: Your alkyne fact-sheet
First member ethyne $C_2H_2$; H-C-C angle $180^\circ$ (linear)
Triple bond = 1 C-C $\sigma$ (sp-sp) + 2 C-C $\pi$ + 2 C-H $\sigma$
Lengths: $C{\equiv}C = 120 \lt C{=}C = 133 \lt C{-}C = 154$ pm (shortest, strongest)
Acidity (terminal H): $HC{\equiv}CH \gt H_2C{=}CH_2 \gt CH_3CH_3$ ($sp \gt sp^2 \gt sp^3$)
Markovnikov governs HX & water addition; $Br_2/CCl_4$ decolourised (unsaturation test)

segments.text: Let us pin down the alkyne facts you must be able to reproduce on demand.
The general formula is C n H two n minus two for one triple bond in an acyclic chain.
The first member is ethyne, C two H two, and the H C C angle is one hundred eighty degrees, so the molecule is strictly linear.
The triple bond is one carbon carbon sigma from s p to s p overlap, plus two carbon carbon pi bonds, plus the two C H sigma bonds.

Bond enthalpies: the triple bond, about eight hundred twenty three, beats the double bond, about six hundred eighty one, which beats the single bond, about three hundred forty eight kilojoules per mole.

And lengths run the other way: the triple bond is one hundred twenty picometres, shorter than the double at one hundred thirty three and the single at one hundred fifty four. It is the shortest, strongest C C bond of the chapter.
Acidity of the terminal hydrogen runs ethyne greater than ethene greater than ethane, tracking s p greater than s p two greater than s p three s-character.
And the signature: ethyne plus sodium gives monosodium ethynide plus half a mole of hydrogen.
Markovnikov's rule governs H X and water addition to unsymmetrical alkynes, and orange bromine in carbon tetrachloride is decolourised on addition, the usual unsaturation test.
चलो वो alkyne facts pin करें जो आपको demand पर reproduce करने आने चाहिए।
General formula एक acyclic chain में एक triple bond के लिए C n H two n minus two है।
पहला member ethyne है, C two H two, और H C C angle एक सौ अस्सी degrees है, तो molecule बिल्कुल linear है।
Triple bond एक carbon carbon sigma है, s p से s p overlap से, plus दो carbon carbon pi bonds, plus दो C H sigma bonds।
Bond enthalpies: triple bond, लगभग आठ सौ तेईस, double bond से बड़ा, लगभग छह सौ इक्यासी, जो single bond से बड़ा, लगभग तीन सौ अड़तालीस kilojoules per mole।
और lengths उल्टी चलती हैं: triple bond एक सौ बीस picometres है, double के एक सौ तैंतीस और single के एक सौ चौवन से छोटा। ये chapter का सबसे छोटा, सबसे strong C C bond है।
Terminal hydrogen की acidity चलती है ethyne, ethene से बड़ा, ethene, ethane से, s p, s p two से बड़ा, s p two, s p three से वाला s-character track करते हुए।
और signature: ethyne plus sodium, monosodium ethynide plus आधा mole hydrogen देता है।
Markovnikov का rule unsymmetrical alkynes में H X और water addition को govern करता है, और carbon tetrachloride में orange bromine addition पर decolourise हो जाता है, वही unsaturation test।

Two $sp$ orbitals point $180^\circ$ apart: one C-C $\sigma$, one C-H $\sigma$
Two leftover p orbitals stand perpendicular to the axis and to each other

board_events.text: The two perpendicular pairs overlap sideways to make two $\pi$ bonds
The molecule is strictly linear (H-C-C-H on one line)
Two $\pi$ clouds = an electron-rich cylinder, with room to add twice

segments.text: Under the hood, each carbon of ethyne is s p hybridised, and that geometry explains both the shape and the acidity.
Two s p orbitals point one hundred eighty degrees apart, one forming the carbon carbon sigma bond and the other a C H sigma bond.
The two leftover unhybridised p orbitals on each carbon stand perpendicular to the axis and to each other.
They overlap sideways to make two pi bonds, one pair up and down, the other in front and behind, wrapping the axis in a cylindrical sheath.
So the electron cloud from these two pi bonds is cylindrically symmetric about the bond axis.
And because the two s p orbitals sit at one hundred eighty degrees, the molecule is strictly linear: H, carbon, carbon, H all on one line.
So the takeaway is a picture: two pi clouds forming an electron-rich cylinder that electrophiles love, with room to add a reagent twice.
Hood के नीचे, ethyne का हर carbon s p hybridised है, और वो geometry shape और acidity दोनों समझा देती है।
दो s p orbitals एक सौ अस्सी degrees अलग की ओर इशारा करते हैं, एक carbon carbon sigma bond बनाता है और दूसरा C H sigma bond।
हर carbon पर दो बचे unhybridised p orbitals axis के और एक-दूसरे के perpendicular खड़े रहते हैं।
वो sideways overlap करके दो pi bonds बनाते हैं, एक जोड़ी ऊपर-नीचे, दूसरी आगे-पीछे, axis को एक cylindrical sheath में लपेटते हुए।
तो इन दो pi bonds से बना electron cloud bond axis के around cylindrically symmetric है।
और क्योंकि दोनों s p orbitals एक सौ अस्सी degrees पर बैठते हैं, molecule बिल्कुल linear है: H, carbon, carbon, H सब एक line पर।
तो takeaway एक तस्वीर है: दो pi clouds जो एक electron-rich cylinder बनाते हैं जिसे electrophiles पसंद करते हैं, और जहाँ किसी reagent को दो बार add करने की जगह है।

board_events.text: Naming alkynes
Common: derivatives of acetylene (methylacetylene); IUPAC: -ane $\to$ -yne
$HC{\equiv}CH$ ethyne; $CH_3C{\equiv}CH$ propyne; then but-1-yne and but-2-yne
Ethyne and propyne have only one structure each
From butyne onward: position isomerism (but-1-yne vs but-2-yne)
Larger members also show chain isomerism (the $C_5H_8$ set)
Recognising position vs chain isomers quickly saves time in exams

segments.text: Naming alkynes uses two systems, and both are worth recognising.
In the common system they are named as derivatives of acetylene, like methylacetylene. In I U P A C, you replace the a n e of the parent alkane with y n e.
So H C triple bond C H is ethyne, C H three C triple bond C H is propyne, and the two four-carbon alkynes are but-one-yne and but-two-yne.
Ethyne and propyne each have only one possible structure.
From butyne onward, alkynes show position isomerism, as in but-one-yne versus but-two-yne.
And larger members show chain isomerism too: the C five H eight set is pent-one-yne, pent-two-yne, and three-methylbut-one-yne.
Being able to spot position versus chain isomers quickly is a small skill that saves real time in the exam.
Alkynes को name करने में दो systems इस्तेमाल होते हैं, और दोनों को पहचानना फ़ायदेमंद है।
Common system में इन्हें acetylene के derivatives की तरह name करते हैं, जैसे methylacetylene। I U P A C में, आप parent alkane के a n e को y n e से replace करते हैं।
तो H C triple bond C H ethyne है, C H three C triple bond C H propyne है, और दो four-carbon alkynes but-one-yne और but-two-yne हैं।
Ethyne और propyne में से हर एक की सिर्फ एक possible structure है।
Butyne से आगे, alkynes position isomerism दिखाते हैं, जैसे but-one-yne बनाम but-two-yne।
और larger members chain isomerism भी दिखाते हैं: C five H eight set है pent-one-yne, pent-two-yne, और three-methylbut-one-yne।
Position बनाम chain isomers को जल्दी पहचान लेना एक छोटी skill है जो exam में असली वक़्त बचाती है।

board_events.text: Alkynes follow the family trend
First three members gases; next eight liquids; higher members solids
Weakly polar, lighter than water, immiscible with water
Soluble in organic solvents (ether, $CCl_4$, benzene)
Melting point, boiling point, and density all rise with molar mass
Ethyne is a colourless gas with a characteristic odour; higher members odourless
The triple bond announces itself in chemistry, not in melting and boiling

segments.text: Physically, alkynes follow the same trend as the alkanes and alkenes before them.
The first three members are gases, the next eight are liquids, and the higher members are solids.
They are weakly polar, lighter than water, and immiscible with it.
They dissolve well in organic solvents such as ether, carbon tetrachloride, and benzene.
Melting point, boiling point, and density all rise with molar mass, exactly as before.
Ethyne itself is a colourless gas with a characteristic odour, while the higher members are essentially odourless.
So in bulk physical behaviour, alkynes differ little from the families already studied. The triple bond announces itself in chemistry, not in melting and boiling.
Physically, alkynes उसी trend को follow करते हैं जो उनसे पहले alkanes और alkenes की थी।
पहले तीन members gases हैं, अगले आठ liquids हैं, और higher members solids हैं।
ये weakly polar हैं, पानी से हल्के, और उसके साथ immiscible।
ये organic solvents में अच्छे से घुल जाते हैं, जैसे ether, carbon tetrachloride, और benzene।
Melting point, boiling point, और density सब molar mass के साथ बढ़ते हैं, बिल्कुल पहले की तरह।
Ethyne ख़ुद एक colourless gas है जिसकी एक characteristic गंध होती है, जबकि higher members असल में odourless हैं।
तो bulk physical behaviour में, alkynes पहले पढ़ी families से कम ही अलग हैं। Triple bond ख़ुद को chemistry में जताता है, melting और boiling में नहीं।

board_events.text: Two routes to an alkyne
(a) Calcium carbide (industrial): drop water on $CaC_2$
Limestone $\to$ quick lime $\to$ carbide $\to$ ethyne on contact with water
(b) From vicinal dihalides: two eliminations
Alcoholic KOH removes the first HX $\to$ a vinyl (alkenyl) halide
Sodamide ($NaNH_2$) removes the second HX $\to$ the triple bond
Match base to difficulty: alc. KOH for the first, stronger $NaNH_2$ for the second

segments.text: There are two routes worth knowing to an alkyne: one industrial, one a two-step elimination.
Route a is industrial. Ethyne is made on scale by simply dropping water on calcium carbide.
The whole chain starts from limestone: heating gives quick lime, fusing that with coke gives calcium carbide, and the carbide liberates ethyne the moment it meets water.
This is why old acetylene lamps and oxy-acetylene welding sets ran on lumps of carbide and a steady drip of water.
Route b starts from a vicinal dihalide and takes two elimination steps.
Alcoholic potassium hydroxide removes the first molecule of H X, giving an alkenyl, or vinyl, halide.
Then the much stronger base sodamide removes the second H X from that vinyl halide, unveiling the triple bond.
The two-step base sequence matters: alcoholic potassium hydroxide is strong enough for the first elimination, but the second, from a vinyl halide, needs the much stronger sodamide.
एक alkyne तक पहुँचने के दो routes जानने लायक़ हैं: एक industrial, एक two-step elimination।
Route a industrial है। Ethyne बड़े पैमाने पर बस calcium carbide पर पानी डालकर बनाया जाता है।
पूरी chain limestone से शुरू होती है: गरम करने पर quick lime मिलता है, उसे coke के साथ fuse करने पर calcium carbide, और carbide पानी से मिलते ही ethyne छोड़ देता है।
यही वजह है कि पुराने acetylene lamps और oxy-acetylene welding sets carbide के टुकड़ों और पानी की लगातार बूँदों पर चलते थे।
Route b एक vicinal dihalide से शुरू होता है और दो elimination steps लेता है।
Alcoholic potassium hydroxide H X का पहला molecule हटाता है, एक alkenyl, यानी vinyl, halide देता है।
फिर कहीं ज़्यादा strong base sodamide उस vinyl halide से दूसरा H X हटाता है, triple bond उजागर करते हुए।
Two-step base sequence मायने रखता है: alcoholic potassium hydroxide पहले elimination के लिए काफ़ी strong है, लेकिन दूसरा, एक vinyl halide से, कहीं ज़्यादा strong sodamide माँगता है।

sections.title: The signature reaction: acidity and acetylides

board_events.text: Acetylides: the terminal-alkyne fingerprint
Na and sodamide are strong bases; they deprotonate the terminal H
Alkenes and alkanes do NOT react this way $\Rightarrow$ the test distinguishes a terminal alkyne
Reason: the $sp$ carbon's 50% s-character stabilises the negative charge left behind
Ethyne has two acidic H's; excess Na gives the disodium ethynide
Order: $HC{\equiv}CH \gt CH_3C{\equiv}CH \gt CH_3C{\equiv}CCH_3$ (last has no acidic H)

segments.text: <excited>Now the signature reaction: acetylide formation, the fingerprint of a terminal alkyne.
Sodium metal and sodamide are strong bases. They deprotonate the terminal hydrogen of ethyne, releasing hydrogen gas and forming a metal acetylide.
Ethyne plus sodium gives monosodium ethynide plus half a mole of hydrogen.
And propyne with sodamide gives sodium propynide plus ammonia.
Because alkenes and alkanes do not react this way, the test cleanly distinguishes a terminal alkyne from alkenes, alkanes, and even internal alkynes.
The reason is hybridisation: the s p carbon's high s-character, fifty percent, makes it electronegative enough to stabilise the negative charge left behind, so the proton departs easily.
Ethyne carries two acidic hydrogens, one on each carbon, so with an excess of sodium it can be deprotonated twice, giving the disodium ethynide.
So monosodium ethynide plus more sodium gives disodium ethynide plus another half mole of hydrogen.
And within the alkynes, acidity runs ethyne greater than propyne greater than but-two-yne, the last having no acidic hydrogen at all.
<excited>अब signature reaction: acetylide formation, एक terminal alkyne का fingerprint।
Sodium metal और sodamide strong bases हैं। ये ethyne के terminal hydrogen को deprotonate करते हैं, hydrogen gas release करते हुए और एक metal acetylide बनाते हुए।
Ethyne plus sodium monosodium ethynide plus आधा mole hydrogen देता है।
और propyne sodamide के साथ sodium propynide plus ammonia देता है।
क्योंकि alkenes और alkanes इस तरह react नहीं करते, ये test एक terminal alkyne को alkenes, alkanes, और यहाँ तक कि internal alkynes से साफ़ अलग कर देता है।
वजह hybridisation है: s p carbon का ऊँचा s-character, पचास percent, उसे इतना electronegative बना देता है कि वो पीछे छूटे negative charge को stabilise कर सके, इसलिए proton आसानी से चला जाता है।
Ethyne दो acidic hydrogens carry करता है, हर carbon पर एक, तो sodium की अधिकता के साथ इसे दो बार deprotonate किया जा सकता है, disodium ethynide देते हुए।
तो monosodium ethynide plus और sodium, disodium ethynide plus एक और आधा mole hydrogen देता है।
और alkynes के भीतर, acidity चलती है ethyne, propyne से बड़ा, propyne, but-two-yne से, आख़िरी में तो कोई acidic hydrogen है ही नहीं।

sections.title: Electrophilic addition I: hydrogen and halogens

board_events.text: Two $\pi$ bonds means two additions
For unsymmetrical alkynes this follows Markovnikov's rule
Dihydrogen over Ni/Pd/Pt: alkyne $\to$ alkene $\to$ alkane
Stop at the alkene: Lindlar $\to$ cis; Na/liq. $NH_3$ $\to$ trans
Halogens add in two stages: dihalo-alkene, then tetrahalide
Why twice? The first addition makes a double bond; the second saturates it

segments.text: Because it has two pi bonds, an alkyne adds two molecules of most reagents, the orientation set by the more stable intermediate, a vinylic cation.
For unsymmetrical alkynes this follows Markovnikov's rule, exactly as developed for alkenes.
Dihydrogen over nickel, palladium, or platinum reduces the alkyne first to the alkene and then all the way to the alkane.
So ethyne goes to ethene, and ethene to ethane.

Stop the reduction at the alkene with the controlled catalysts from the alkene sub-topic: Lindlar for the cis alkene, sodium in liquid ammonia for the trans. That is why preparation from alkynes appears there too.
Halogens add in two stages: chlorine or bromine gives first a dihalo-alkene and then a tetrahalide.
So ethyne plus bromine gives dibromoethene, and a second bromine gives one-one-two-two-tetrabromoethane.
Why does an alkyne consume two molecules where an alkene takes one? Simply because it has two pi bonds: the first addition makes a double bond, and the second saturates it.
क्योंकि इसके पास दो pi bonds हैं, एक alkyne ज़्यादातर reagents के दो molecules add करता है, orientation ज़्यादा stable intermediate, एक vinylic cation, से तय होती है।
Unsymmetrical alkynes के लिए ये Markovnikov के rule को follow करता है, ठीक वैसे जैसे alkenes के लिए बनाया गया था।
Nickel, palladium, या platinum पर dihydrogen alkyne को पहले alkene तक और फिर पूरी तरह alkane तक reduce करता है।
तो ethyne, ethene में जाता है, और ethene, ethane में।
Reduction को alkene पर रोको alkene sub-topic वाले controlled catalysts से: cis alkene के लिए Lindlar, trans के लिए liquid ammonia में sodium। यही वजह है कि alkynes से preparation वहाँ भी आता है।
Halogens दो stages में add होते हैं: chlorine या bromine पहले एक dihalo-alkene देता है और फिर एक tetrahalide।
तो ethyne plus bromine, dibromoethene देता है, और दूसरा bromine, one-one-two-two-tetrabromoethane देता है।
एक alkyne दो molecules क्यों लेता है जहाँ एक alkene एक लेता है? बस इसलिए कि उसके पास दो pi bonds हैं: पहला addition एक double bond बनाता है, और दूसरा उसे saturate कर देता है।

board_events.text: Adding HX twice makes a gem-dihalide
Two molecules of HX add (Markovnikov), both halogens on the SAME carbon
For propyne, both bromines land on the central carbon $\to$ 2,2-dibromopropane
gem = both X on one carbon (from HX); vicinal = X on adjacent carbons (from one $X_2$)
Orientation follows Markovnikov through the more stable vinylic cation
Track the reagent: 2 HX gives gem; one $X_2$ gives vicinal

segments.text: Hydrogen halides also add twice, and where they land is the key exam point.
Two molecules of H X add, following Markovnikov each time, and both halogens end up on the same carbon, giving a gem-dihalide.
So ethyne plus two H B r gives one-one-dibromoethane.
For propyne, both bromines land on the central, more substituted carbon, giving two-two-dibromopropane.
Keep the two apart: a gem-dihalide has both halogens on one carbon and comes from adding H X, while a vicinal dihalide has them on adjacent carbons and comes from a single halogen molecule.
And each addition follows Markovnikov through the more stable vinylic cation, which is what funnels both halogens onto the same carbon.
So the memory rule is: track the reagent. Two H X gives gem; one halogen molecule gives vicinal.
Hydrogen halides भी दो बार add होते हैं, और वो कहाँ बैठते हैं, यही key exam point है।
H X के दो molecules add होते हैं, हर बार Markovnikov follow करते हुए, और दोनों halogens एक ही carbon पर आ जाते हैं, एक gem-dihalide देते हुए।
तो ethyne plus दो H B r, one-one-dibromoethane देता है।
Propyne के लिए, दोनों bromines central, ज़्यादा substituted carbon पर आते हैं, two-two-dibromopropane देते हुए।

दोनों को अलग रखो: एक gem-dihalide में दोनों halogens एक carbon पर होते हैं और ये H X add करने से आता है, जबकि एक vicinal dihalide में वो adjacent carbons पर होते हैं और ये एक halogen molecule से आता है।
और हर addition ज़्यादा stable vinylic cation से होकर Markovnikov follow करता है, यही दोनों halogens को एक ही carbon पर पहुँचाता है।
तो memory rule है: reagent को track करो। दो H X gem देता है; एक halogen molecule vicinal देता है।

board_events.text: Adding water: the carbonyl surprise
Alkynes don't react with water alone; need $HgSO_4$ in dilute $H_2SO_4$ at 333 K
One water adds (Markovnikov); the unstable enol rearranges to a carbonyl

board_events.text: Ethyne is the special case: it gives the aldehyde acetaldehyde
Every higher alkyne gives a KETONE, not an alcohol; never stop at the enol

segments.text: <curious>The famous hydration product is a genuine surprise: adding water to an alkyne gives a carbonyl compound, not an alcohol.
Alkynes do not react with water alone. They need mercuric sulphate in dilute sulphuric acid at three hundred thirty three kelvin.
One molecule of water adds, Markovnikov fashion, and the unstable enol first formed rearranges to a carbonyl compound.
Here is the scheme for ethyne: water adds under the mercury catalyst, the enol forms, and it tautomerises to acetaldehyde.
Ethyne is the special case. Because both its carbons are identical and each keeps a hydrogen, the product is the aldehyde acetaldehyde.
So ethyne plus water under the mercury catalyst gives acetaldehyde.
But every higher alkyne gives a ketone, because the carbon receiving the hydroxyl has no hydrogen left after tautomerisation. The rule: never stop at the enol.
<curious>मशहूर hydration product एक सच्ची surprise है: एक alkyne में पानी add करने से एक carbonyl compound मिलता है, alcohol नहीं।
Alkynes अकेले पानी से react नहीं करते। इन्हें dilute sulphuric acid में mercuric sulphate चाहिए, तीन सौ तैंतीस kelvin पर।
पानी का एक molecule add होता है, Markovnikov तरीक़े से, और पहले बना unstable enol एक carbonyl compound में rearrange हो जाता है।
ये रहा ethyne के लिए scheme: mercury catalyst के तहत पानी add होता है, enol बनता है, और वो acetaldehyde में tautomerise हो जाता है।
Ethyne special case है। क्योंकि इसके दोनों carbons एक जैसे हैं और हर एक एक hydrogen रखता है, product aldehyde acetaldehyde है।
तो ethyne plus पानी mercury catalyst के तहत acetaldehyde देता है।
लेकिन हर higher alkyne एक ketone देता है, क्योंकि hydroxyl पाने वाले carbon पर tautomerisation के बाद कोई hydrogen नहीं बचता। Rule: कभी enol पर मत रुको।

board_events.text: Two polymerisations of ethyne
Linear polymerisation $\to$ polyacetylene (polyethyne)
A polyene of repeating $-(CH{=}CH)-$ units
Suitably treated, it conducts electricity
Cyclic polymerisation: three molecules through a red-hot tube $\to$ benzene
That cyclic route is the natural bridge into the arenes of Sub-04

segments.text: Ethyne polymerises in two very different ways, and each opens a door beyond this chapter.
Under suitable conditions, ethyne undergoes linear polymerisation to polyacetylene, also called polyethyne.
It is a high-molecular-weight polyene of repeating C H double bond C H units.
When suitably treated, this polyene conducts electricity, and it is the basis of conducting-polymer research.
Ethyne also undergoes cyclic polymerisation. Passed through a red-hot tube, three molecules combine to form benzene.
So three ethyne molecules over a red-hot iron tube at about eight hundred seventy three kelvin give benzene.
And that cyclic route is the natural bridge into the aromatic hydrocarbons, the arenes, of the next sub-topic.
Ethyne दो बहुत अलग तरीक़ों से polymerise होता है, और हर एक इस chapter से आगे एक दरवाज़ा खोलता है।
सही conditions में, ethyne linear polymerisation करके polyacetylene बनाता है, जिसे polyethyne भी कहते हैं।
ये एक high-molecular-weight polyene है जिसमें C H double bond C H units दोहराती हैं।
सही तरीक़े से treat करने पर, ये polyene बिजली conduct करता है, और ये conducting-polymer research का आधार है।
Ethyne cyclic polymerisation भी करता है। एक red-hot tube से गुज़ारने पर, तीन molecules मिलकर benzene बनाते हैं।
तो तीन ethyne molecules एक red-hot iron tube पर लगभग आठ सौ तिहत्तर kelvin पर benzene देते हैं।
और वो cyclic route अगले sub-topic के aromatic hydrocarbons, यानी arenes, में एक natural bridge है।

board_events.text: [C B S E] Propyne + (i) $NaNH_2$ (ii) water/$HgSO_4$
Propyne, $CH_3C{\equiv}CH$, is a terminal alkyne
(i) The terminal C-H is acidic; sodamide removes it
Product: sodium propynide (sodium prop-1-ynide)
(ii) Markovnikov hydration: water's O to the more substituted carbon; enol $\to$ ketone
Product: propanone (acetone)

segments.text: A clean C B S E question. Write the products when propyne reacts with sodamide and with water in the presence of mercuric sulphate and dilute sulphuric acid.
Propyne is C H three C triple bond C H, a terminal alkyne, so it has an acidic hydrogen.
In part one, the terminal C H is acidic, and the strong base sodamide removes it.
Propyne plus sodamide gives sodium propynide plus ammonia.
So the first product is sodium propynide, also written sodium prop-one-ynide.
In part two, Markovnikov hydration puts water's oxygen on the more substituted carbon, and the enol rearranges to a ketone.
Propyne plus water under the mercury catalyst gives propanone.
So the second product is propanone, better known as acetone.
एक clean C B S E सवाल। लिखो कि propyne, sodamide के साथ और mercuric sulphate व dilute sulphuric acid की मौजूदगी में पानी के साथ react करने पर क्या products देता है।
Propyne, C H three C triple bond C H है, एक terminal alkyne, तो इसमें एक acidic hydrogen है।
Part one में, terminal C H acidic है, और strong base sodamide उसे हटा देता है।
Propyne plus sodamide, sodium propynide plus ammonia देता है।
तो पहला product sodium propynide है, जिसे sodium prop-one-ynide भी लिखते हैं।
Part two में, Markovnikov hydration पानी का oxygen ज़्यादा substituted carbon पर रखता है, और enol एक ketone में rearrange हो जाता है।
Propyne plus पानी mercury catalyst के तहत propanone देता है।
तो दूसरा product propanone है, जिसे acetone के नाम से बेहतर जानते हैं।

board_events.text: [N E E T] Which liberates $H_2$ with sodium?
Single rule: only a hydrogen on a triply-bonded carbon is acidic enough to react
(A) but-2-yne $CH_3C{\equiv}CCH_3$: triple bond internal, no terminal H $\to$ no reaction
(B) but-1-yne $CH_3CH_2C{\equiv}CH$: has a terminal C-H $\to$ reacts, liberates $H_2$
(C) but-2-ene: only $sp^2$ and $sp^3$ C-H, not acidic $\to$ no reaction
Answer: only (B) but-1-yne
Trap: seeing 'yne' in (A) and assuming any alkyne reacts

segments.text: A classic N E E T speed trap. Which of three compounds liberates hydrogen gas on treatment with sodium metal?
Do not write mechanisms. Apply the single rule: only a hydrogen sitting on a triply-bonded carbon is acidic enough to react with sodium.
Candidate A, but-two-yne: the triple bond is internal, with no terminal C H, so there is no reaction.
Candidate B, but-one-yne: it has a terminal C H, so it reacts and liberates hydrogen.
Candidate C, but-two-ene: it has only s p two and s p three C H, which are not acidic, so no reaction.
So the answer is only B, but-one-yne.
The trap is seeing y n e in A and assuming any alkyne reacts, forgetting the hydrogen must sit on the triple-bonded carbon.
एक classic N E E T speed trap। तीन compounds में से कौन sodium metal के साथ treat करने पर hydrogen gas छोड़ता है?
Mechanisms मत लिखो। एक ही rule लगाओ: सिर्फ वो hydrogen जो एक triply-bonded carbon पर बैठा हो, sodium से react करने लायक़ acidic होता है।
Candidate A, but-two-yne: triple bond internal है, कोई terminal C H नहीं, तो कोई reaction नहीं।
Candidate B, but-one-yne: इसमें एक terminal C H है, तो ये react करता है और hydrogen छोड़ता है।
Candidate C, but-two-ene: इसमें सिर्फ s p two और s p three C H हैं, जो acidic नहीं हैं, तो कोई reaction नहीं।
तो जवाब है सिर्फ B, but-one-yne।
Trap है A में y n e देखकर मान लेना कि कोई भी alkyne react करता है, ये भूलकर कि hydrogen triple-bonded carbon पर होना चाहिए।

board_events.text: [J E E Main] Hydration regiochemistry + iodoform
(i) Why ethyne $\to$ aldehyde but every higher alkyne $\to$ ketone?
Markovnikov puts -OH on the more substituted carbon
In ethyne both carbons keep an H $\to$ enol $\to$ acetaldehyde (an aldehyde)
In a higher alkyne the -OH carbon has no H after tautomerisation $\to$ ketone
(ii) But-1-yne hydrates at $C_2$ $\to$ butan-2-one
Butan-2-one has a $CH_3CO-$ (methyl ketone) group $\to$ positive iodoform test

segments.text: A multi-concept J E E Main problem, joining the ethyne exception to the iodoform test.
Part one asks why hydration of ethyne gives an aldehyde while every higher alkyne gives a ketone.
Markovnikov hydration places the hydroxyl on the more substituted carbon.
In ethyne both carbons are identical and each keeps a hydrogen, so the enol rearranges to acetaldehyde, and the carbonyl carbon still holds a hydrogen, making it an aldehyde.
In any higher alkyne, the carbon receiving the hydroxyl is bonded to a carbon chain, so after tautomerisation it has no hydrogen, and the product is a ketone.
Part two: but-one-yne undergoes Markovnikov hydration at carbon two, giving butan-two-one.
So but-one-yne plus water under the mercury catalyst gives butan-two-one.
And butan-two-one contains a methyl ketone group, C H three C O, so it gives a positive iodoform test.
एक multi-concept J E E Main problem, जो ethyne exception को iodoform test से जोड़ती है।
Part one पूछता है कि ethyne का hydration aldehyde क्यों देता है जबकि हर higher alkyne ketone देता है।
Markovnikov hydration hydroxyl को ज़्यादा substituted carbon पर रखता है।
Ethyne में दोनों carbons एक जैसे हैं और हर एक एक hydrogen रखता है, तो enol acetaldehyde में rearrange होता है, और carbonyl carbon अब भी एक hydrogen पकड़े रहता है, जो उसे aldehyde बनाता है।
किसी भी higher alkyne में, hydroxyl पाने वाला carbon एक carbon chain से जुड़ा होता है, तो tautomerisation के बाद उस पर कोई hydrogen नहीं होता, और product एक ketone होता है।
Part two: but-one-yne carbon two पर Markovnikov hydration करता है, butan-two-one देते हुए।
तो but-one-yne plus पानी mercury catalyst के तहत butan-two-one देता है।
और butan-two-one में एक methyl ketone group है, C H three C O, तो ये positive iodoform test देता है।

board_events.text: [J E E Advanced] pKa and choosing a base
Given pKa: ethyne $\approx 25$, $NH_3 \approx 38$, water $\approx 16$, ethene $\approx 44$, ethane $\approx 50$
(i) Lower pKa = stronger acid $\to$ acidity ethyne $\gt$ ethene $\gt$ ethane
The carbanion is most stable in the highest-s-character orbital ($sp$)
(ii) A base works only if its conjugate acid is WEAKER (higher pKa) than the substrate
$NaNH_2$: conjugate acid $NH_3$ (38) $\gt$ alkyne (25) $\to$ CAN form the acetylide
NaOH: conjugate acid water (16) $\lt$ alkyne (25) $\to$ CANNOT deprotonate the alkyne
(iii) Make acetylides with $NaNH_2$ or Na metal, never with hydroxide

segments.text: A J E E Advanced favourite that ties acidity to the choice of base, using pKa values.
The given p K a values are: ethyne about twenty-five, ammonia about thirty-eight, water about sixteen, ethene about forty-four, and ethane about fifty.
Part one: lower p K a means a stronger acid, so acidity runs ethyne, twenty-five, greater than ethene, forty-four, greater than ethane, fifty.
The conjugate base, the carbanion, is most stable when its lone pair sits in the orbital of highest s-character, the s p orbital, which holds the electrons closest to the nucleus.
Part two uses a rule: a base can deprotonate an acid only if the base's conjugate acid is weaker, that is, higher in p K a, than the substrate.
For sodamide, the conjugate acid is ammonia, p K a thirty-eight, which is weaker than the alkyne at twenty-five, so sodamide can form the acetylide.
For sodium hydroxide, the conjugate acid is water, p K a sixteen, which is stronger than the alkyne, so hydroxide cannot deprotonate the alkyne to any useful extent.

So part three: acetylides must be made with a strong enough base such as sodamide or sodium metal, never with hydroxide. That is why sodamide is specified for both the second elimination and acetylide formation.
एक J E E Advanced favourite जो acidity को base के चुनाव से जोड़ती है, pKa values इस्तेमाल करके।
दिए गए p K a values हैं: ethyne लगभग पच्चीस, ammonia लगभग अड़तीस, water लगभग सोलह, ethene लगभग चवालीस, और ethane लगभग पचास।
Part one: कम p K a मतलब ज़्यादा strong acid, तो acidity चलती है ethyne, पच्चीस, ethene से बड़ा, चवालीस, ethene, ethane से, पचास।
Conjugate base, यानी carbanion, तब सबसे stable होता है जब उसका lone pair सबसे ऊँचे s-character वाले orbital में बैठे, यानी s p orbital, जो electrons को nucleus के सबसे पास रखता है।
Part two एक rule इस्तेमाल करता है: एक base किसी acid को तभी deprotonate कर सकता है जब base का conjugate acid weaker हो, यानी p K a में ऊँचा, substrate से।
Sodamide के लिए, conjugate acid ammonia है, p K a अड़तीस, जो alkyne के पच्चीस से weaker है, तो sodamide acetylide बना सकता है।
Sodium hydroxide के लिए, conjugate acid पानी है, p K a सोलह, जो alkyne से stronger है, तो hydroxide alkyne को किसी काम की हद तक deprotonate नहीं कर सकता।

तो part three: acetylides को काफ़ी strong base से बनाना चाहिए जैसे sodamide या sodium metal, कभी hydroxide से नहीं। यही वजह है कि sodamide दूसरे elimination और acetylide formation दोनों के लिए बताया जाता है।

board_events.text: Four traps that cost marks on alkynes
Trap 1: calling all alkynes acidic
Point to the actual H: it must sit on a triply-bonded carbon. 'No terminal H, no acetylide'
Trap 2: writing an alcohol as the hydration product
Pro-Tip: 'ethyne $\to$ aldehyde, all others $\to$ ketone'; never stop at the enol
Trap 3: confusing gem- and vicinal dihalides
Trap 4: NaOH is too weak for acetylides; use $NaNH_2$ or Na (conjugate acid must be weaker)

segments.text: Let us close alkynes with the four pitfalls that quietly cost the most marks.
Trap one, calling all alkynes acidic. Internal alkynes, with no terminal C H, form no acetylide at all.
Pro tip: before applying the sodium test, point to the actual hydrogen. It must sit directly on a triply-bonded carbon. No terminal hydrogen, no acetylide.
Trap two, writing an alcohol as the hydration product. Alkyne plus water gives a carbonyl, because the enol tautomerises.
Pro tip: remember, ethyne gives an aldehyde, all others give a ketone. And never stop at the enol.
Trap three, confusing gem and vicinal dihalides. Adding two H X gives a gem-dihalide, both halogens on one carbon; adding one halogen molecule gives a vicinal one, spread across the bond.

Trap four, using sodium hydroxide to make acetylides. Hydroxide is too weak, because water is more acidic than the alkyne. Use sodamide or sodium metal: a base works only if its conjugate acid is weaker than the substrate.
चलो alkynes को उन चार pitfalls के साथ बंद करें जो चुपचाप सबसे ज़्यादा marks खा जाते हैं।
Trap one, सारे alkynes को acidic कह देना। Internal alkynes, जिनमें कोई terminal C H नहीं, कोई acetylide बनाते ही नहीं।
Pro tip: sodium test लगाने से पहले, असली hydrogen की ओर इशारा करो। वो सीधे एक triply-bonded carbon पर होना चाहिए। कोई terminal hydrogen नहीं, तो कोई acetylide नहीं।
Trap two, hydration product को alcohol लिख देना। Alkyne plus पानी एक carbonyl देता है, क्योंकि enol tautomerise हो जाता है।
Pro tip: याद रखो, ethyne aldehyde देता है, बाक़ी सब ketone देते हैं। और कभी enol पर मत रुको।
Trap three, gem और vicinal dihalides को गड्डमड्ड करना। दो H X add करना gem-dihalide देता है, दोनों halogens एक carbon पर; एक halogen molecule add करना vicinal देता है, bond के आर-पार फैला।

Trap four, acetylides बनाने के लिए sodium hydroxide इस्तेमाल करना। Hydroxide बहुत weak है, क्योंकि पानी alkyne से ज़्यादा acidic है। Sodamide या sodium metal इस्तेमाल करो: एक base तभी काम करता है जब उसका conjugate acid substrate से weaker हो।

board_events.text: Aromatic: a name for a deeper stability
The flagship: benzene $C_6H_6$, a flat ring, each C with one H
Its formula is hydrogen-poor: your alkene instincts should rebel
It should decolourise $Br_2$ water and Baeyer's reagent, but it does not
It refuses addition and prefers substitution, keeping the ring intact
Something is protecting that ring: this whole sub-topic explains what
A recurring theme returns: aromaticity resists addition

segments.text: <curious>The word aromatic began as a description of smell, because many early such compounds were fragrant. But chemistry kept the word for a deeper reason: a special, almost stubborn stability.
The flagship is benzene, C six H six, six carbons in a flat ring, each bonded to a single hydrogen.
Look at that formula and your alkene instincts should rebel. It is enormously hydrogen-poor, so it looks like it should be packed with double bonds.
By that logic it should decolourise bromine water and Baeyer's reagent on contact, the way every alkene and alkyne does. Yet benzene does almost none of this.
It refuses to add bromine across a double bond, it survives Baeyer's reagent, and instead of adding, it prefers to substitute, swapping a ring hydrogen for a new group while keeping the ring intact.
So something is clearly protecting that ring. This whole sub-topic is the story of what that protection is, and how it shapes every reaction.
And it brings back the chapter's theme one last time: unsaturation invites addition, but aromaticity resists it.
<curious>शब्द aromatic गंध के वर्णन से शुरू हुआ, क्योंकि शुरुआती ऐसे कई compounds ख़ुशबूदार थे। लेकिन chemistry ने ये शब्द एक गहरी वजह से रखा: एक ख़ास, लगभग ज़िद्दी stability।
Flagship benzene है, C six H six, एक flat ring में छह carbons, हर एक एक single hydrogen से bonded।
उस formula को देखो और आपकी alkene instincts को बग़ावत करनी चाहिए। ये बेहद hydrogen-poor है, तो लगता है इसमें double bonds भरे होने चाहिए।
उस logic से इसे छूते ही bromine water और Baeyer's reagent को decolourise कर देना चाहिए, जैसे हर alkene और alkyne करता है। फिर भी benzene लगभग कुछ नहीं करता।

ये double bond के across bromine add करने से इनकार करता है, Baeyer's reagent झेल जाता है, और add करने के बजाय substitute करना पसंद करता है, ring को बरक़रार रखते हुए एक ring hydrogen की जगह नया group लाता है।
तो कुछ तो साफ़ तौर पर उस ring की रक्षा कर रहा है। ये पूरा sub-topic इसी की कहानी है कि वो रक्षा क्या है, और कैसे वो हर reaction को आकार देती है।
और ये chapter की theme को आख़िरी बार वापस लाता है: unsaturation addition को invite करती है, लेकिन aromaticity उसे resist करती है।

sections.title: The delocalised doughnut and resonance energy

board_events.text: Six $\pi$ electrons as one continuous doughnut
Each carbon is $sp^2$ with one perpendicular p orbital
All six p orbitals overlap sideways into one delocalised cloud
Delocalisation lowers the energy: shared electrons beat localised double bonds
So benzene is far more stable than an imaginary 'cyclohexatriene'
All arene chemistry flows from that resonance energy

segments.text: Think about it this way: picture the six pi electrons not as three fixed double bonds, but as a single continuous doughnut of electron density spread evenly above and below the flat ring.
Each carbon is s p two hybridised, contributing one unhybridised p orbital perpendicular to the ring.
All six of those p orbitals overlap sideways into a single delocalised cloud, so the electrons are shared by all six carbons rather than pinned between two.
Sharing the electrons over all six carbons lowers the energy, which is exactly why the delocalised ring is more stable than any set of localised double bonds.
Because of that sharing, the molecule is far more stable than any imaginary cyclohexatriene with alternating fixed bonds would be.
That extra stability is the resonance energy, about one hundred fifty kilojoules per mole for benzene.

And this is the single fact from which all of arene chemistry flows: reactions that would destroy the delocalised ring, that is addition, are resisted, while reactions that preserve it, substitution, are favoured.
इसे ऐसे सोचो: छह pi electrons को तीन fixed double bonds की तरह नहीं, बल्कि electron density के एक continuous doughnut की तरह देखो जो flat ring के ऊपर और नीचे एक जैसा फैला है।
हर carbon s p two hybridised है, एक unhybridised p orbital देता है जो ring के perpendicular है।
वो छहों p orbitals sideways overlap करके एक single delocalised cloud बनाते हैं, तो electrons दो carbons के बीच बँधे रहने के बजाय छहों carbons में बँटे होते हैं।
Electrons को छहों carbons पर बाँटना energy को कम करता है, यही वजह है कि delocalised ring किसी भी localised double bonds के set से ज़्यादा stable है।
उस sharing की वजह से, molecule किसी भी काल्पनिक cyclohexatriene से, जिसमें alternating fixed bonds हों, कहीं ज़्यादा stable है।
वो extra stability resonance energy है, benzene के लिए लगभग एक सौ पचास kilojoules per mole।
और यही वो एक fact है जिससे arene की सारी chemistry बहती है: जो reactions delocalised ring को नष्ट कर दें, यानी addition, वो resist होती हैं, जबकि जो उसे बचाएँ, substitution, वो favoured होती हैं।
