board_events.text: So the bonds are neither single nor double, but one intermediate order everywhere
There are no 'real' double bonds; the hybrid is the reality
Hexagon-with-a-circle is the honest picture of benzene

segments.text: The historical clue to all this was the bonds themselves. Kekule first drew benzene as a ring with alternating single and double bonds.
But experiment shows all six carbon carbon bonds are identical, each one hundred thirty nine picometres long.
That length sits neatly between a single bond at one hundred fifty four picometres and a double bond at one hundred thirty four.

So there are no real double bonds to find. The true structure is a resonance hybrid of Kekule's two equivalent drawings, best shown as a hexagon with a circle inside, and edge-on, a pi doughnut above and below the plane.
So the six bonds are neither single nor double: they are one intermediate bond order, identical all the way round the ring.
The two Kekule forms are just equivalent contributors on paper. The real molecule is their hybrid, with one identical, delocalised set of bonds.
So the hexagon with a circle inside is the honest picture of benzene, a reminder that the six pi electrons belong to the whole ring, not to three fixed bonds.
इस सबका historical सुराग़ ख़ुद bonds में था। Kekule ने पहले benzene को alternating single और double bonds वाली ring की तरह बनाया।
लेकिन experiment दिखाता है कि सभी छह carbon carbon bonds एक जैसे हैं, हर एक एक सौ उनतालीस picometres लंबा।
वो length एक single bond, एक सौ चौवन picometres, और एक double bond, एक सौ चौंतीस, के बीच बिल्कुल ठीक बैठती है।

तो कोई असली double bonds मिलते ही नहीं। असली structure Kekule के दो equivalent चित्रों का एक resonance hybrid है, जिसे एक circle वाले hexagon से सबसे अच्छा दिखाया जाता है, और edge-on देखने पर, plane के ऊपर-नीचे एक pi doughnut।
तो छहों bonds न single हैं न double: वो एक intermediate bond order हैं, ring के चारों ओर एक जैसे।
दोनों Kekule forms काग़ज़ पर बस equivalent contributors हैं। असली molecule उनका hybrid है, जिसमें एक जैसे, delocalised bonds का एक set है।
तो अंदर circle वाला hexagon benzene की ईमानदार तस्वीर है, एक याददहानी कि छह pi electrons पूरी ring के हैं, तीन fixed bonds के नहीं।

sections.title: Huckel's rule: what makes a ring aromatic

board_events.text: Aromatic is more than 'a ring with double bonds'
A compound is aromatic if it is cyclic, planar, and fully conjugated
...and it contains $(4n+2)$ delocalised $\pi$ electrons (Huckel's rule)
Benzene satisfies it with $n=1$: six $\pi$ electrons
Benzene can be forced to add only under vigorous conditions
Ordinary unsaturation tests FAIL for arenes: a key diagnostic

segments.text: Be precise about what aromatic means. It is not simply a ring with some double bonds. There are four conditions, all required.
A compound is aromatic only if it is cyclic, planar, and fully conjugated, so the p orbitals can overlap continuously around the ring.
And it must contain four n plus two delocalised pi electrons, where n is a whole number. That is Huckel's rule.
Written compactly: aromatic if and only if cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, with four n plus two pi electrons.
Benzene satisfies the rule with n equal to one, giving six pi electrons, four times one plus two.
You can force benzene to add, by hydrogenation or by chlorination in ultraviolet light, but only under vigorous conditions that overpower the aromatic stability.
And the ordinary tests for unsaturation, bromine water and Baeyer's reagent, fail for arenes. That failure is itself a key diagnostic that distinguishes benzene from alkenes and alkynes.
Aromatic का मतलब क्या है, इसमें precise रहो। ये बस कुछ double bonds वाली ring नहीं है। चार conditions हैं, सब ज़रूरी।
एक compound तभी aromatic है जब वो cyclic, planar, और fully conjugated हो, ताकि p orbitals ring के around लगातार overlap कर सकें।
और उसमें four n plus two delocalised pi electrons होने चाहिए, जहाँ n एक पूर्ण संख्या है। यही Huckel का rule है।
संक्षेप में लिखें तो: aromatic तभी और केवल तभी जब cyclic, planar, fully conjugated हो, और four n plus two pi electrons हों।
Benzene इस rule को n बराबर one के साथ satisfy करता है, जिससे छह pi electrons मिलते हैं, four गुणा one plus two।
आप benzene को add करने के लिए मजबूर कर सकते हो, hydrogenation से या ultraviolet light में chlorination से, लेकिन सिर्फ vigorous conditions में जो aromatic stability को हरा दें।
और unsaturation के ordinary tests, bromine water और Baeyer's reagent, arenes के लिए fail होते हैं। वो failure ख़ुद एक key diagnostic है जो benzene को alkenes और alkynes से अलग करता है।

board_events.text: Your arene fact-sheet
Benzene: planar hexagon, $sp^2$, all C-C $=139$ pm, all angles $120^\circ$, six delocalised $\pi$
Characteristic reaction: electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS)
Activating, o/p-directing: $-OH, -NH_2, -OR, -CH_3, -C_6H_5$ (electron-donating)
Deactivating, o/p-directing: the halogens $-F, -Cl, -Br, -I$ (the exception)
Deactivating, m-directing: $-NO_2, -CN, -CHO, -COOH, -SO_3H$ (electron-withdrawing)

segments.text: Let us pin the arene facts you must reproduce on demand.
The benzene series has the general formula C n H two n minus six, for n six or more, with benzene itself C six H six.
Benzene is a planar regular hexagon, every carbon s p two, all carbon carbon bonds one hundred thirty nine picometres, all angles one hundred twenty degrees, with six delocalised pi electrons.
Its resonance energy, the stabilisation from delocalisation, is about one hundred fifty kilojoules per mole.
The characteristic reaction is electrophilic aromatic substitution, in which an electrophile replaces a ring hydrogen while preserving aromaticity.
Activating, ortho para directing groups are the electron donors: hydroxyl, amino, alkoxy, methyl and other alkyls, and phenyl.
The halogens are the exception: they are deactivating, they slow the ring, yet they still direct the electrophile to ortho and para.
Deactivating, meta directing groups are the electron withdrawers: nitro, cyano, aldehyde, carboxyl, and sulphonic acid groups.
चलो वो arene facts pin करें जो आपको demand पर reproduce करने आने चाहिए।
Benzene series का general formula C n H two n minus six है, n छह या ज़्यादा के लिए, और benzene ख़ुद C six H six।
Benzene एक planar regular hexagon है, हर carbon s p two, सभी carbon carbon bonds एक सौ उनतालीस picometres, सभी angles एक सौ बीस degrees, छह delocalised pi electrons के साथ।
इसकी resonance energy, delocalisation से मिली stabilisation, लगभग एक सौ पचास kilojoules per mole है।
Characteristic reaction electrophilic aromatic substitution है, जिसमें एक electrophile aromaticity को बचाते हुए एक ring hydrogen को replace करता है।
Activating, ortho para directing groups electron donors हैं: hydroxyl, amino, alkoxy, methyl और दूसरे alkyls, और phenyl।
Halogens exception हैं: ये deactivating हैं, ring को धीमा करते हैं, फिर भी electrophile को ortho और para की ओर direct करते हैं।
Deactivating, meta directing groups electron withdrawers हैं: nitro, cyano, aldehyde, carboxyl, और sulphonic acid groups।

board_events.text: Where arenes sit, and how we name them
Many keep trivial names: toluene, aniline, phenol
Disubstituted rings use ortho (1,2), meta (1,3), para (1,4)
Ring as a substituent = phenyl ($C_6H_5-$); ring plus $CH_2$ = benzyl
aryl (Ar-) is the general term for any aromatic group
Positional isomerism: the three xylenes ($C_8H_{10}$)
Recognising o/m/p quickly is the same skill the directive-influence section needs

segments.text: Aromatic hydrocarbons are the third great family of the chapter, alongside the open-chain aliphatics and the alicyclic cycloalkanes.
Many benzene derivatives keep trivial names: toluene for methylbenzene, aniline for aminobenzene, and phenol for hydroxybenzene.
Disubstituted benzenes use the prefixes ortho for one two, meta for one three, and para for one four.
The ring as a substituent is the phenyl group, C six H five. It is worth distinguishing phenyl from benzyl, which is the ring plus a C H two, and aryl is the general term for any aromatic group.
And aryl, written A r, is the general term for any aromatic group, the aromatic analogue of alkyl. These names recur throughout organic chemistry.
Disubstituted rings also show positional isomerism: the three dimethylbenzenes, the ortho, meta, and para xylenes, share the formula C eight H ten but differ in the placement of the two methyls.
Recognising ortho, meta, and para relationships quickly is exactly the skill the directive-influence section will demand, so it is worth drilling now.
Aromatic hydrocarbons chapter की तीसरी बड़ी family हैं, open-chain aliphatics और alicyclic cycloalkanes के साथ।
कई benzene derivatives trivial names रखते हैं: methylbenzene के लिए toluene, aminobenzene के लिए aniline, और hydroxybenzene के लिए phenol।
Disubstituted benzenes prefixes इस्तेमाल करते हैं: one two के लिए ortho, one three के लिए meta, और one four के लिए para।
Substituent के तौर पर ring, phenyl group है, C six H five। Phenyl को benzyl से अलग समझना ज़रूरी है, जो ring plus एक C H two है, और aryl किसी भी aromatic group के लिए general term है।
और aryl, जिसे A r लिखते हैं, किसी भी aromatic group के लिए general term है, alkyl का aromatic analogue। ये नाम पूरी organic chemistry में बार-बार आते हैं।
Disubstituted rings positional isomerism भी दिखाती हैं: तीन dimethylbenzenes, यानी ortho, meta, और para xylenes, formula C eight H ten share करते हैं लेकिन दोनों methyls की जगह में फ़र्क़ रखते हैं।
Ortho, meta, और para रिश्तों को जल्दी पहचानना ठीक वही skill है जो directive-influence section माँगेगा, तो इसे अभी drill करना फ़ायदेमंद है।

board_events.text: Three laboratory routes to benzene
(a) Cyclic polymerisation of ethyne over a red-hot iron tube
(b) Decarboxylation of sodium benzoate with soda lime
(c) Reduction of phenol over heated zinc dust
$C_6H_5OH + Zn \rightarrow C_6H_6 + ZnO$

segments.text: There are three laboratory routes to benzene worth knowing.
Route a is the cyclic polymerisation of ethyne, forward-pointed from the alkyne sub-topic.
Three molecules of ethyne, passed through a red-hot iron tube at about eight hundred seventy three kelvin, cyclise to benzene.
Route b is decarboxylation. Heating the sodium salt of benzoic acid with soda lime strips the carboxyl as carbonate, leaving benzene.
So sodium benzoate with soda lime gives benzene plus sodium carbonate.
Route c is reduction of phenol. Phenol vapours passed over heated zinc dust are reduced to benzene.
That is phenol plus zinc gives benzene plus zinc oxide. Three routes, one product: the aromatic ring itself.
Benzene तक पहुँचने के तीन laboratory routes जानने लायक़ हैं।
Route a ethyne का cyclic polymerisation है, alkyne sub-topic से आगे की ओर इशारा किया हुआ।
Ethyne के तीन molecules, एक red-hot iron tube से लगभग आठ सौ तिहत्तर kelvin पर गुज़ारे जाएँ, तो benzene में cyclise हो जाते हैं।
Route b decarboxylation है। Benzoic acid के sodium salt को soda lime के साथ गरम करने से carboxyl carbonate की तरह निकल जाता है, benzene छोड़ते हुए।
तो sodium benzoate soda lime के साथ benzene plus sodium carbonate देता है।
Route c phenol का reduction है। Phenol के vapours गरम zinc dust पर से गुज़ारे जाएँ तो benzene में reduce हो जाते हैं।
यानी phenol plus zinc, benzene plus zinc oxide देता है। तीन routes, एक product: ख़ुद aromatic ring।

sections.title: Physical properties and the evidence for resonance

board_events.text: Non-polar, sooty-flamed, and toxic
Their signature is a sooty, luminous flame (high carbon-to-hydrogen ratio)
Benzene is also toxic, a point returned to at the sub-topic's end
How do we know the ring is extra-stable? Heat of hydrogenation
Cyclohexene releases ~120 kJ/mol; a 'cyclohexatriene' should give ~360
Benzene releases far less; the shortfall $\approx 150$ kJ/mol is the resonance energy
That measured number matches the resonance energy quoted earlier

segments.text: Benzene and its homologues are non-polar molecules: colourless liquids or low-melting solids, immiscible with water, and lighter than it.
Their most distinctive everyday signature is the sooty, luminous flame they give on burning, a direct result of a high carbon to hydrogen ratio leaving unburnt carbon glowing.
Benzene is also toxic, a point we return to at the very end of this sub-topic.
But how do we know the ring carries that extra stability? The cleanest evidence is the heat of hydrogenation.

Hydrogenating cyclohexene, with one double bond, releases about one hundred twenty kilojoules per mole, so a hypothetical cyclohexatriene with three isolated double bonds should release roughly three times that, about three hundred sixty.

But benzene actually releases far less than that estimate. The shortfall, around one hundred fifty kilojoules per mole, is precisely the resonance energy, the energy benzene did not have to give up because it was extra-stable to begin with.
And that number, measured this way, matches the resonance energy we quoted earlier. It is the quantitative backbone of the whole idea of aromatic stability.
Benzene और उसके homologues non-polar molecules हैं: colourless liquids या low-melting solids, पानी के साथ immiscible, और उससे हल्के।
इनकी सबसे ख़ास रोज़मर्रा पहचान है जलने पर मिलने वाली sooty, luminous flame, जो high carbon to hydrogen ratio का सीधा नतीजा है, जो बिना जले carbon को दहकता छोड़ देती है।
Benzene toxic भी है, एक बात जिस पर हम इस sub-topic के बिल्कुल आख़िर में लौटेंगे।
लेकिन हमें कैसे पता कि ring वो extra stability रखती है? सबसे साफ़ सबूत heat of hydrogenation है।

Cyclohexene को, जिसमें एक double bond है, hydrogenate करने पर लगभग एक सौ बीस kilojoules per mole निकलते हैं, तो एक काल्पनिक cyclohexatriene जिसमें तीन isolated double bonds हों, उसे लगभग तीन गुना, यानी करीब तीन सौ साठ, देना चाहिए।
लेकिन benzene असल में उस अनुमान से कहीं कम देता है। वो कमी, लगभग एक सौ पचास kilojoules per mole, ठीक resonance energy है, वो energy जो benzene को देनी नहीं पड़ी क्योंकि वो शुरू से ही extra-stable था।
और वो संख्या, इस तरह मापी गई, उस resonance energy से match करती है जो हमने पहले बताई थी। ये पूरी aromatic stability की सोच की quantitative रीढ़ है।

board_events.text: Forming the arenium ion is the slow, rate-determining step
Step 3: a base plucks $H^+$ off the $sp^3$ carbon, restoring aromaticity
The ring 'pays' in step 2 and 'recovers' in step 3, so it substitutes not adds

segments.text: <excited>Every important reaction of benzene shares one three-step mechanism. Learn it once, and the individual reactions become variations on a theme.
Step one: a reagent plus a catalyst generates a strong electrophile, E plus, such as the nitronium ion or a carbocation.
Step two: the pi cloud attacks E plus. One carbon becomes s p three and the positive charge spreads over the remaining five carbons as a resonance-stabilised arenium ion.
Here is the general scheme: make the electrophile, form the arenium ion where aromaticity is temporarily lost, and then restore it.
Forming the arenium ion is the slow, rate-determining step, because aromaticity is temporarily lost, which costs energy.
Step three: a base plucks the proton off the s p three carbon, the electrons fall back into the ring, and the aromatic sextet is regenerated, giving the substituted benzene.
So the ring pays to host the electrophile in step two and recovers its stability in step three. That is exactly why benzene substitutes rather than adds.
<excited>Benzene की हर अहम reaction एक ही three-step mechanism share करती है। इसे एक बार सीख लो, और अलग-अलग reactions एक theme की variations बन जाती हैं।
Step one: एक reagent plus एक catalyst एक strong electrophile बनाते हैं, E plus, जैसे nitronium ion या एक carbocation।
Step two: pi cloud E plus पर हमला करता है। एक carbon s p three बन जाता है और positive charge बाक़ी पाँच carbons पर एक resonance-stabilised arenium ion की तरह फैल जाता है।
ये रहा general scheme: electrophile बनाओ, arenium ion बनाओ जहाँ aromaticity अस्थायी तौर पर खो जाती है, और फिर उसे वापस लाओ।
Arenium ion बनाना धीमा, rate-determining step है, क्योंकि aromaticity अस्थायी तौर पर खो जाती है, जिसकी energy की क़ीमत लगती है।
Step three: एक base s p three carbon से proton खींच लेता है, electrons वापस ring में गिर जाते हैं, और aromatic sextet फिर से बन जाता है, substituted benzene देते हुए।
तो ring step two में electrophile को रखने की क़ीमत चुकाती है और step three में अपनी stability वापस पा लेती है। ठीक इसीलिए benzene add करने के बजाय substitute करता है।

sections.title: Five substitutions I: nitration and halogenation

board_events.text: The five substitutions, first two
Nitration: conc. $HNO_3$ in conc. $H_2SO_4$ at 323-333 K $\to$ nitrobenzene
Halogenation: $Cl_2$ or $Br_2$ with anhydrous $FeCl_3$ or $AlCl_3$
Always name the ELECTROPHILE: $NO_2^+$, $Cl^+$, not $HNO_3$ or $Cl_2$

segments.text: The three-step mechanism now plays out as five named reactions. Take the first two: nitration and halogenation.
Nitration: benzene with concentrated nitric acid in concentrated sulphuric acid at three hundred twenty three to three hundred thirty three kelvin gives nitrobenzene.
The electrophile is the nitronium ion, N O two plus, generated when sulphuric acid protonates nitric acid.
So benzene plus nitric acid, in concentrated sulphuric acid, gives nitrobenzene plus water.
Halogenation: benzene with chlorine or bromine and a Lewis-acid catalyst, anhydrous ferric chloride or aluminium chloride, gives chlorobenzene.
The catalyst polarises the halogen to deliver chlorine plus, so benzene plus chlorine gives chlorobenzene plus H C l.
One habit to build: in a mechanism, always name the electrophile itself, nitronium or chlorine plus, not the starting reagents nitric acid or chlorine.
Three-step mechanism अब पाँच named reactions की तरह सामने आता है। पहली दो लो: nitration और halogenation।
Nitration: benzene concentrated nitric acid के साथ concentrated sulphuric acid में तीन सौ तेईस से तीन सौ तैंतीस kelvin पर nitrobenzene देता है।
Electrophile nitronium ion है, N O two plus, जो तब बनता है जब sulphuric acid, nitric acid को protonate करता है।
तो benzene plus nitric acid, concentrated sulphuric acid में, nitrobenzene plus water देता है।
Halogenation: benzene chlorine या bromine और एक Lewis-acid catalyst, anhydrous ferric chloride या aluminium chloride के साथ, chlorobenzene देता है।
Catalyst halogen को polarise करके chlorine plus देता है, तो benzene plus chlorine, chlorobenzene plus H C l देता है।
एक आदत बनानी है: mechanism में, हमेशा electrophile का नाम लो, nitronium या chlorine plus, न कि starting reagents nitric acid या chlorine।

sections.title: Five substitutions II: sulphonation and Friedel-Crafts

board_events.text: Sulphonation, and the two Friedel-Crafts reactions
Sulphonation: benzene + oleum $\to$ benzenesulphonic acid (reversible)
Friedel-Crafts alkylation: benzene + $RCl$/anhyd. $AlCl_3$ (electrophile $R^+$)
Friedel-Crafts acylation: benzene + $RCOCl$/anhyd. $AlCl_3$ (electrophile $RCO^+$)
$C_6H_6 + CH_3COCl \to$ acetophenone; acylation avoids polyalkylation & rearrangement

segments.text: Now the remaining three: sulphonation and the two Friedel-Crafts reactions.
Sulphonation: benzene heated with fuming sulphuric acid, oleum, gives benzenesulphonic acid. The electrophile is sulphur trioxide, and the reaction is notably reversible.
So benzene plus oleum is in equilibrium with benzenesulphonic acid plus water.
Friedel-Crafts alkylation: benzene with an alkyl halide and anhydrous aluminium chloride attaches an alkyl group; the electrophile is the carbocation R plus.
So benzene plus methyl chloride gives toluene plus H C l.
Friedel-Crafts acylation: benzene with an acyl chloride and anhydrous aluminium chloride attaches an acyl group; the electrophile is the acylium ion, R C O plus.
So benzene plus acetyl chloride gives acetophenone. Acylation is cleaner than alkylation: the acylium ion does not rearrange, and the ketone product is deactivated, so it stops at mono-substitution.
अब बाक़ी तीन: sulphonation और दो Friedel-Crafts reactions।
Sulphonation: benzene fuming sulphuric acid, यानी oleum, के साथ गरम करने पर benzenesulphonic acid देता है। Electrophile sulphur trioxide है, और reaction ख़ास तौर पर reversible है।
तो benzene plus oleum, benzenesulphonic acid plus water के साथ equilibrium में रहता है।
Friedel-Crafts alkylation: benzene एक alkyl halide और anhydrous aluminium chloride के साथ एक alkyl group जोड़ता है; electrophile carbocation R plus है।
तो benzene plus methyl chloride, toluene plus H C l देता है।
Friedel-Crafts acylation: benzene एक acyl chloride और anhydrous aluminium chloride के साथ एक acyl group जोड़ता है; electrophile acylium ion है, R C O plus।

तो benzene plus acetyl chloride, acetophenone देता है। Acylation, alkylation से cleaner है: acylium ion rearrange नहीं होता, और ketone product deactivated होता है, तो ये mono-substitution पर रुक जाता है।

board_events.text: Under force, benzene will add and burn
$C_6H_6 + 3Cl_2$ in UV $\to$ benzene hexachloride (BHC, lindane)
Both need vigorous conditions that overpower the resonance stability
Benzene burns with a sooty, luminous flame (high C-to-H ratio)
Addition breaks aromaticity; that is why substitution is the norm

segments.text: Under forcing conditions, benzene can be made to add, sacrificing its aromaticity.
Benzene plus three hydrogen over nickel, at four hundred seventy three to five hundred twenty three kelvin, gives cyclohexane.
And benzene plus three chlorine in ultraviolet light gives benzene hexachloride, once used as the insecticide lindane.
Both additions need vigorous conditions, precisely because they must overpower the resonance stability that normally protects the ring.
Combustion: two benzene plus fifteen oxygen give twelve carbon dioxide plus six water.
And benzene burns with that sooty, luminous flame, because of its high carbon to hydrogen ratio, a quick visual test for an aromatic.
So addition always breaks aromaticity, and that is the deepest reason substitution, not addition, is the norm for the whole family.
Forcing conditions में, benzene को add करने के लिए मजबूर किया जा सकता है, अपनी aromaticity क़ुर्बान करते हुए।
Benzene plus तीन hydrogen, nickel पर, चार सौ तिहत्तर से पाँच सौ तेईस kelvin पर, cyclohexane देता है।
और benzene plus तीन chlorine ultraviolet light में benzene hexachloride देता है, जो कभी insecticide lindane के तौर पर इस्तेमाल होता था।
दोनों additions को vigorous conditions चाहिए, ठीक इसलिए कि उन्हें उस resonance stability को हराना पड़ता है जो आम तौर पर ring की रक्षा करती है।
Combustion: दो benzene plus पंद्रह oxygen, बारह carbon dioxide plus छह water देते हैं।
और benzene उसी sooty, luminous flame के साथ जलता है, अपने high carbon to hydrogen ratio की वजह से, किसी aromatic के लिए एक झटपट visual test।
तो addition हमेशा aromaticity तोड़ता है, और यही सबसे गहरी वजह है कि substitution, न कि addition, पूरी family के लिए norm है।

sections.title: Directive influence: where does the next group go?

board_events.text: An existing group decides speed and position
Ortho/para-directing groups push electron density into the ring
For a donor, o/p attack lets the substituent stabilise the positive charge
Meta attack offers a donor no such help, so o/p wins and the ring is activated
Meta-directing groups pull electron density out and are deactivating
For a withdrawer, o/p puts positive charge next to an electron-poor carbon
The reasoning is always arenium-ion stability: draw the resonance structures

segments.text: When benzene already carries a substituent, that group decides both how fast the ring reacts and where the next electrophile attaches. Two families emerge.
Ortho para directing groups push electron density into the ring, stabilising the arenium ion when attack is at the ortho and para positions.

For an electron-donating group, attack at ortho and para produces an arenium ion with a contributor where the positive charge sits on the carbon bearing the group, exactly where a lone pair or an electron-rich alkyl can stabilise it.
Meta attack offers a donor no such help, because no resonance structure puts the positive charge on the substituted carbon, so ortho and para win and the whole ring is activated.
Meta directing groups do the opposite: they pull electron density out of the ring, are deactivating, and leave the meta arenium ion the least destabilised.
For an electron-withdrawing group, that same ortho para contributor places positive charge next to an already electron-poor carbon, strongly destabilising it, so the least-bad option is meta.

So the reasoning is always the same: draw the arenium-ion resonance structures for ortho, meta, and para attack, and see which positions let the substituent help, for donors, or least hurt, for withdrawers.
जब benzene पहले से एक substituent रखता है, वो group दोनों तय करता है: ring कितनी तेज़ react करेगी और अगला electrophile कहाँ जुड़ेगा। दो families उभरती हैं।
Ortho para directing groups ring में electron density धकेलते हैं, arenium ion को stabilise करते हुए जब हमला ortho और para positions पर हो।

एक electron-donating group के लिए, ortho और para पर हमला एक arenium ion बनाता है जिसमें एक contributor ऐसा होता है जहाँ positive charge उस carbon पर होता है जिस पर group है, ठीक वहाँ जहाँ एक lone pair या electron-rich alkyl उसे stabilise कर सके।
Meta हमला किसी donor को ऐसी कोई मदद नहीं देता, क्योंकि कोई resonance structure positive charge को substituted carbon पर नहीं रखता, तो ortho और para जीतते हैं और पूरी ring activated होती है।
Meta directing groups उल्टा करते हैं: ये ring से electron density खींचते हैं, deactivating होते हैं, और meta arenium ion को सबसे कम destabilised छोड़ते हैं।
एक electron-withdrawing group के लिए, वही ortho para contributor positive charge को पहले से electron-poor carbon के बगल रख देता है, उसे strongly destabilise करते हुए, तो सबसे कम बुरा विकल्प meta है।

तो reasoning हमेशा एक ही है: ortho, meta, और para हमले के लिए arenium-ion resonance structures बनाओ, और देखो कौन सी positions substituent को मदद करने देती हैं, donors के लिए, या सबसे कम नुक़सान, withdrawers के लिए।

sections.title: Activating, deactivating, and the halogen exception

board_events.text: Two effects, sometimes pulling opposite ways
Activating o/p: $-OH, -NH_2, -OR, -CH_3$ and other alkyls
Deactivating m-directing: $-NO_2, -COOH, -CHO, -SO_3H, -CN$
Halogens: deactivating (via $-I$) yet o/p-directing (via $+R$)
Rule of thumb: donors activate and send o/p; withdrawers deactivate and send meta
Friedel-Crafts fails on strongly deactivated rings (e.g. nitrobenzene)
Alkylation also suffers polyalkylation and carbocation rearrangement

segments.text: Grouping the directors: most ortho para directors are activating, faster than benzene, but there is one famous exception.
The activating ortho para directors are the electron donors: hydroxyl, amino, alkoxy, methyl, and other alkyl groups.
The deactivating meta directors are the electron withdrawers: nitro, carboxyl, aldehyde, sulphonic acid, and cyano groups.
The halogens are the exception. Their strong minus I effect makes them deactivating, slower than benzene, yet their lone-pair donation by resonance still steers the electrophile to ortho and para.
So the rule of thumb is simple: electron donors activate the ring and send the next group ortho and para; electron withdrawers deactivate it and send the next group meta.

A practical footnote: Friedel-Crafts reactions fail on strongly deactivated rings. Nitrobenzene, for instance, undergoes neither Friedel-Crafts alkylation nor acylation, because the ring is too electron-poor.

Alkylation suffers two more problems: polyalkylation, because the first alkyl group is activating, and carbocation rearrangement, because a primary R plus can shift to a more stable cation. Acylation avoids both.
Directors को समूह में बाँटें: ज़्यादातर ortho para directors activating हैं, benzene से तेज़, लेकिन एक मशहूर exception है।
Activating ortho para directors electron donors हैं: hydroxyl, amino, alkoxy, methyl, और दूसरे alkyl groups।
Deactivating meta directors electron withdrawers हैं: nitro, carboxyl, aldehyde, sulphonic acid, और cyano groups।
Halogens exception हैं। उनका strong minus I effect उन्हें deactivating बनाता है, benzene से धीमा, फिर भी उनका resonance से lone-pair donation electrophile को ortho और para की ओर steer करता है।
तो rule of thumb आसान है: electron donors ring को activate करते हैं और अगले group को ortho और para भेजते हैं; electron withdrawers उसे deactivate करते हैं और अगले group को meta भेजते हैं।

एक practical footnote: Friedel-Crafts reactions strongly deactivated rings पर fail होती हैं। Nitrobenzene, मिसाल के तौर पर, न Friedel-Crafts alkylation करता है न acylation, क्योंकि ring बहुत electron-poor है।

Alkylation दो और समस्याएँ झेलता है: polyalkylation, क्योंकि पहला alkyl group activating होता है, और carbocation rearrangement, क्योंकि एक primary R plus ज़्यादा stable cation में shift हो सकता है। Acylation दोनों से बच जाता है।

board_events.text: The chapter closes on a sober note
Polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) form when organic matter burns incompletely
Sources: tobacco smoke, vehicle exhaust, coal soot, char-grilled food
Many PAHs are carcinogenic: metabolised into DNA-damaging species
The damage is indirect: the body's metabolism makes the reactive, DNA-attacking form
Benzene itself is toxic and a recognised carcinogen on prolonged exposure
A real-world reason the aromatic ring matters beyond the exam hall

segments.text: The chapter closes on a sober, real-world note about the arenes.
Polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons, or P A Hs, are fused-ring aromatics produced whenever organic matter burns incompletely.
You meet them in tobacco smoke, vehicle exhaust, coal soot, and char-grilled food. Benzo a pyrene is a well-known example.
Many P A Hs are carcinogenic. Once absorbed, they are metabolised in the body into species that can damage D N A.
The damage is indirect: it is the body's own metabolism that converts an absorbed P A H into the reactive species which then attacks D N A.
Benzene itself is toxic and a recognised carcinogen with prolonged exposure, which is why it is handled with care in the laboratory.
So incomplete-combustion sources are a genuine public-health concern, a direct, real-world reason the aromatic ring matters far beyond the exam hall.
Chapter arenes के बारे में एक गंभीर, असल-दुनिया वाली बात पर बंद होता है।
Polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons, यानी P A Hs, fused-ring aromatics हैं जो तब बनते हैं जब organic matter अधूरे तौर पर जलता है।
आप इन्हें tobacco smoke, vehicle exhaust, coal soot, और char-grilled food में मिलते हो। Benzo a pyrene एक जाना-पहचाना उदाहरण है।
कई P A Hs carcinogenic हैं। एक बार absorb होने पर, ये शरीर में ऐसी species में metabolise हो जाते हैं जो D N A को नुक़सान पहुँचा सकती हैं।
नुक़सान अप्रत्यक्ष है: ये शरीर का अपना metabolism है जो एक absorb हुए P A H को reactive species में बदलता है, जो फिर D N A पर हमला करती है।
Benzene ख़ुद toxic है और लंबे exposure के साथ एक recognised carcinogen, यही वजह है कि इसे laboratory में सावधानी से handle किया जाता है।
तो incomplete-combustion के स्रोत एक सच्ची public-health चिंता हैं, एक सीधी, असल-दुनिया वाली वजह कि aromatic ring exam hall से कहीं आगे मायने रखती है।

board_events.text: [C B S E] Nitration of benzene
Conditions: conc. $HNO_3$ with conc. $H_2SO_4$ at 323-333 K
Electrophile: the nitronium ion $NO_2^+$
The nitronium ion attacks the ring, then a base removes $H^+$
Product: nitrobenzene

segments.text: A clean C B S E question. Write the equation, the conditions, and the active electrophile for the nitration of benzene, and name the product.
The reagents and conditions are concentrated nitric acid with concentrated sulphuric acid, the nitrating mixture, at three hundred twenty three to three hundred thirty three kelvin.
The active electrophile is the nitronium ion, N O two plus.
It is generated by sulphuric acid protonating nitric acid, as shown.
The equation is benzene plus nitric acid, in concentrated sulphuric acid, giving the product plus water.
Mechanistically, the nitronium ion attacks the ring to form the arenium ion, then a base removes the proton to restore aromaticity.
So the product is nitrobenzene. The key marks are the electrophile and the concentrated-acid conditions.
एक clean C B S E सवाल। benzene के nitration के लिए equation, conditions, और active electrophile लिखो, और product का नाम बताओ।
Reagents और conditions हैं concentrated nitric acid के साथ concentrated sulphuric acid, यानी nitrating mixture, तीन सौ तेईस से तीन सौ तैंतीस kelvin पर।
Active electrophile nitronium ion है, N O two plus।
ये sulphuric acid के nitric acid को protonate करने से बनता है, जैसा दिखाया गया है।
Equation है benzene plus nitric acid, concentrated sulphuric acid में, product plus water देते हुए।
Mechanism के हिसाब से, nitronium ion ring पर हमला करके arenium ion बनाता है, फिर एक base proton हटाकर aromaticity वापस लाता है।
तो product nitrobenzene है। Key marks electrophile और concentrated-acid conditions पर हैं।

board_events.text: [N E E T] Nitration of toluene: o/p or meta?
Identify the substituent's class first: $-CH_3$ is an alkyl group
Alkyl is electron-donating $\Rightarrow$ activating and o/p-directing
So nitration is faster than benzene
...and gives mainly o-nitrotoluene and p-nitrotoluene
Answer: o/p products predominate; toluene is more reactive than benzene
Trap: lumping every group together; alkyl is activating, opposite to $-NO_2$

segments.text: A classic N E E T speed trap. Toluene is nitrated. Which products predominate, and is toluene more or less reactive than benzene?
Do not draw mechanisms. Identify the substituent's class first. Methyl is an alkyl group.
An alkyl group is electron-donating, so it is activating and ortho para directing.
So nitration of toluene is faster than nitration of benzene, because the ring is more electron-rich.
And it gives mainly ortho-nitrotoluene and para-nitrotoluene, with little meta.
So the answer: ortho and para products predominate, and toluene is more reactive than benzene.
The trap is lumping every group together. The rule is alkyl equals activating and ortho para, exactly opposite to a nitro group.
एक classic N E E T speed trap। Toluene को nitrate किया जाता है। कौन से products predominate करते हैं, और toluene benzene से ज़्यादा reactive है या कम?
Mechanisms मत बनाओ। पहले substituent की class पहचानो। Methyl एक alkyl group है।
एक alkyl group electron-donating है, तो ये activating और ortho para directing है।
तो toluene का nitration benzene के nitration से तेज़ है, क्योंकि ring ज़्यादा electron-rich है।
और ये मुख्यतः ortho-nitrotoluene और para-nitrotoluene देता है, meta बहुत कम।
तो जवाब: ortho और para products predominate करते हैं, और toluene benzene से ज़्यादा reactive है।
Trap है हर group को एक साथ मान लेना। Rule है alkyl मतलब activating और ortho para, nitro group के बिल्कुल उल्टा।

board_events.text: [J E E Main] Nitrobenzene, nitrated again
$-NO_2$ is strongly electron-withdrawing, hence meta-directing
(i) The second nitro group enters the meta position
(ii) $-NO_2$ deactivates the ring, so it reacts SLOWER than benzene
One idea drives both parts: $-NO_2$ destabilises the o/p arenium ion most
Deactivating + meta-directing: the signature of an electron-withdrawing group

segments.text: A J E E Main problem. Nitrobenzene is treated with a second round of concentrated nitric and sulphuric acid. Predict the position, and the rate relative to benzene.
The nitro group is strongly electron-withdrawing, and therefore meta directing.
So part one: the second nitro group enters the meta position, giving mainly one-three-dinitrobenzene.
So nitrobenzene plus nitric acid gives one-three-dinitrobenzene plus water.
Part two: because the nitro group pulls electron density out of the ring, it deactivates it, so nitrobenzene reacts more slowly than benzene, and the second nitration needs harsher conditions.
A single idea drives both answers: the nitro group destabilises the arenium ion most for ortho and para attack, so the electrophile is funnelled to meta and the whole ring is less nucleophilic.
So deactivating and meta directing together are the signature of an electron-withdrawing group, the exact opposite of the alkyl case.
एक J E E Main problem। Nitrobenzene को concentrated nitric और sulphuric acid के दूसरे दौर के साथ treat किया जाता है। Position predict करो, और benzene के मुक़ाबले rate।
Nitro group strongly electron-withdrawing है, और इसलिए meta directing।
तो part one: दूसरा nitro group meta position में जाता है, मुख्यतः one-three-dinitrobenzene देते हुए।
तो nitrobenzene plus nitric acid, one-three-dinitrobenzene plus water देता है।
Part two: क्योंकि nitro group ring से electron density खींचता है, ये उसे deactivate करता है, तो nitrobenzene benzene से धीमा react करता है, और दूसरे nitration को harsher conditions चाहिए।
एक ही idea दोनों जवाब चलाता है: nitro group ortho और para हमले के लिए arenium ion को सबसे ज़्यादा destabilise करता है, तो electrophile meta की ओर funnel होता है और पूरी ring कम nucleophilic होती है।
तो deactivating और meta directing मिलकर एक electron-withdrawing group की पहचान हैं, alkyl वाले मामले के बिल्कुल उल्टा।

board_events.text: [J E E Advanced] Chlorobenzene's apparent contradiction
Chlorine exerts two opposing electronic effects
A strong $-I$ effect withdraws $\sigma$-electron density, destabilising the cation everywhere
So chlorobenzene is less reactive than benzene (the 'deactivating' label)
A $+R$ effect: chlorine's lone pairs stabilise the o/p arenium ion
The two effects act on different things: speed versus position
$-I$ controls the rate (deactivation); $+R$ controls orientation (o/p) — no contradiction

segments.text: A J E E Advanced favourite. Chlorobenzene undergoes substitution more slowly than benzene, yet the products are predominantly ortho and para. Resolve the apparent contradiction.
The resolution is that chlorine exerts two opposing electronic effects at once.
First, a strong minus I inductive effect. Chlorine is electronegative and withdraws sigma electron density from the ring, destabilising the positive arenium ion at every position.
This makes chlorobenzene less reactive than benzene overall, which is the deactivating label and the slower rate.

Second, a plus R resonance effect. Chlorine's lone pairs can be donated into the ring, and this specifically stabilises the arenium ion for ortho and para attack, where a resonance structure places positive charge on the carbon bearing chlorine.
The crucial insight is that the two effects act on different things: the inductive effect governs speed, the resonance effect governs position.

So there is no real contradiction. The inductive effect dominates the rate, giving overall deactivation, while the resonance effect controls the orientation, giving ortho para. Speed and position are two different things: chlorobenzene is a deactivating, ortho para directing substituent.
एक J E E Advanced favourite। Chlorobenzene benzene से धीमा substitution करता है, फिर भी products मुख्यतः ortho और para होते हैं। इस दिखते विरोधाभास को सुलझाओ।
सुलझाव ये है कि chlorine एक साथ दो opposing electronic effects डालता है।
पहला, एक strong minus I inductive effect। Chlorine electronegative है और ring से sigma electron density खींचता है, हर position पर positive arenium ion को destabilise करते हुए।
इससे chlorobenzene कुल मिलाकर benzene से कम reactive होता है, यही deactivating label और धीमी rate है।

दूसरा, एक plus R resonance effect। Chlorine के lone pairs ring में donate हो सकते हैं, और ये ख़ास तौर पर ortho और para हमले के लिए arenium ion को stabilise करते हैं, जहाँ एक resonance structure positive charge को chlorine वाले carbon पर रखता है।
अहम insight ये है कि दोनों effects अलग चीज़ों पर काम करते हैं: inductive effect speed को govern करता है, resonance effect position को।

तो कोई असली विरोधाभास नहीं है। Inductive effect rate को dominate करता है, कुल deactivation देते हुए, जबकि resonance effect orientation को control करता है, ortho para देते हुए। Speed और position दो अलग चीज़ें हैं: chlorobenzene एक deactivating, ortho para directing substituent है।

board_events.text: Four traps that cost marks on arenes
Trap 1: expecting benzene to decolourise bromine water
Pro-Tip: resists $Br_2$ water and Baeyer's but burns sooty $\Rightarrow$ almost certainly aromatic
Trap 2: calling halogens activating because they are o/p-directing
Pro-Tip: rate is set by induction ($-I$), orientation by resonance ($+R$)
Trap 3: applying $(4n+2)$ without checking the structure
Trap 4: name the ELECTROPHILE ($NO_2^+$, $Cl^+$, $R^+$, $RCO^+$), not the reagent

segments.text: Let us close the arenes with the four pitfalls that quietly cost the most marks.
Trap one, expecting benzene to decolourise bromine water. It does not, because aromaticity blocks ordinary addition.
Pro tip: a compound that resists bromine water and Baeyer's reagent but burns with a sooty flame is almost certainly aromatic.
Trap two, calling halogens activating just because they are ortho para directing. They are the exception: deactivating yet ortho para directing.
Pro tip: for halogens, rate is set by the inductive effect, minus I means slower, while orientation is set by resonance, plus R means ortho para.
Trap three, applying the four n plus two count without checking the structure. The electron count matters only for a cyclic, planar, fully conjugated system.

Trap four, naming the reagent instead of the electrophile. The attacking species is nitronium, chlorine plus, R plus, or acylium, not nitric acid or chlorine themselves. Always write the generated electrophile in mechanism answers.
चलो arenes को उन चार pitfalls के साथ बंद करें जो चुपचाप सबसे ज़्यादा marks खा जाते हैं।
Trap one, ये उम्मीद करना कि benzene bromine water को decolourise करेगा। ये नहीं करता, क्योंकि aromaticity ordinary addition को रोक देती है।
Pro tip: एक compound जो bromine water और Baeyer's reagent झेल जाए लेकिन sooty flame के साथ जले, वो लगभग पक्का aromatic है।
Trap two, halogens को सिर्फ इसलिए activating कह देना कि वो ortho para directing हैं। ये exception हैं: deactivating फिर भी ortho para directing।
Pro tip: halogens के लिए, rate inductive effect से तय होती है, minus I मतलब धीमा, जबकि orientation resonance से तय होती है, plus R मतलब ortho para।
Trap three, structure check किए बिना four n plus two count लगा देना। Electron count सिर्फ एक cyclic, planar, fully conjugated system के लिए मायने रखता है।

Trap four, electrophile के बजाय reagent का नाम लेना। हमला करने वाली species nitronium, chlorine plus, R plus, या acylium है, न कि nitric acid या chlorine ख़ुद। Mechanism के जवाबों में हमेशा बना हुआ electrophile लिखो।

board_events.text: Chapter formula recap
Huckel's rule: aromatic $\Leftrightarrow$ cyclic, planar, conjugated, $(4n+2)\pi$
These formulas anchor the chapter; the cheat sheet turns them into reactions

segments.text: Before the cheat sheet, let us gather the formulas that anchor the whole chapter in one place.
General formulas: an alkane is C n H two n plus two; a cycloalkane, one ring, is C n H two n.
An alkene, one double bond, is C n H two n; an alkyne, one triple bond, is C n H two n minus two.
Alkane combustion: C n H two n plus two plus the quantity three n plus one over two oxygen gives n carbon dioxide plus n plus one water.
Bond enthalpies rise with bond order: single three hundred forty eight, double six hundred eighty one, triple eight hundred twenty three kilojoules per mole.
Terminal-hydrogen acidity: ethyne greater than ethene greater than ethane, tracking s p greater than s p two greater than s p three.
An arene of the benzene series is C n H two n minus six, benzene itself C six H six, with a resonance energy of about one hundred fifty kilojoules per mole.
And Huckel's rule: a species is aromatic if and only if it is cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, with four n plus two pi electrons.
These formulas anchor the whole chapter. The cheat sheet that follows turns them into the reactions and orderings you will actually use.
Cheat sheet से पहले, चलो वो formulas एक जगह इकट्ठा करें जो पूरे chapter को टिकाते हैं।
General formulas: एक alkane, C n H two n plus two है; एक cycloalkane, एक ring, C n H two n है।
एक alkene, एक double bond, C n H two n है; एक alkyne, एक triple bond, C n H two n minus two है।
Alkane combustion: C n H two n plus two plus तीन n plus one बटा two oxygen, n carbon dioxide plus n plus one water देता है।
Bond enthalpies bond order के साथ बढ़ती हैं: single तीन सौ अड़तालीस, double छह सौ इक्यासी, triple आठ सौ तेईस kilojoules per mole।
Terminal-hydrogen acidity: ethyne, ethene से बड़ा, ethene, ethane से, s p, s p two से बड़ा, s p two, s p three से track करते हुए।
Benzene series का एक arene C n H two n minus six है, benzene ख़ुद C six H six, जिसकी resonance energy लगभग एक सौ पचास kilojoules per mole है।
और Huckel का rule: एक species तभी और केवल तभी aromatic है जब वो cyclic, planar, fully conjugated हो, और four n plus two pi electrons हों।
ये formulas पूरे chapter को टिकाते हैं। आगे आने वाला cheat sheet इन्हें उन reactions और orderings में बदल देता है जो आप असल में इस्तेमाल करेंगे।

segments.text: Finally, the one-glance cheat sheet for the whole of Hydrocarbons.
Alkanes: saturated, s p three, paraffins. Make them by hydrogenation, reduction, Wurtz, Kolbe electrolysis, and decarboxylation. Break them by free-radical halogenation and combustion.

Alkenes: s p two, one double bond. Their master reaction is electrophilic addition, Markovnikov by default, with the peroxide effect for H B r only, remember B r breaks the rule. Ozonolysis and cis-trans testing round them out.

Alkynes: s p, linear, with an acidic terminal hydrogen. Key facts: acetylide formation as the terminal-alkyne test, a gem-dihalide from two H X, and Kucherov hydration to a carbonyl, ethyne to aldehyde and all others to ketone.

Arenes: benzene, six pi electrons, resonance energy about one hundred fifty. Their master reaction is electrophilic aromatic substitution in three steps, and they substitute rather than add to preserve aromaticity.
Directive influence in one line: ortho para activating donors like hydroxyl, amino, and methyl; the halogens are ortho para but deactivating; and meta directing deactivators like nitro and carboxyl.

And keep the two alkane orders apart: halogen reactivity fluorine greater than chlorine greater than bromine greater than iodine; hydrogen replacement tertiary greater than secondary greater than primary.
And the mnemonics to carry out of the chapter: staggered equals spread equals stable; B r breaks the rule; and aromatic substitutes, never adds.
आख़िर में, पूरे Hydrocarbons के लिए one-glance cheat sheet।
Alkanes: saturated, s p three, paraffins। इन्हें hydrogenation, reduction, Wurtz, Kolbe electrolysis, और decarboxylation से बनाओ। इन्हें free-radical halogenation और combustion से तोड़ो।

Alkenes: s p two, एक double bond। इनकी master reaction electrophilic addition है, default में Markovnikov, peroxide effect सिर्फ H B r के लिए, याद रखो B r breaks the rule। Ozonolysis और cis-trans testing इन्हें पूरा करते हैं।

Alkynes: s p, linear, एक acidic terminal hydrogen के साथ। Key facts: terminal-alkyne test के तौर पर acetylide formation, दो H X से एक gem-dihalide, और Kucherov hydration से एक carbonyl, ethyne से aldehyde और बाक़ी सब से ketone।

Arenes: benzene, छह pi electrons, resonance energy लगभग एक सौ पचास। इनकी master reaction three steps में electrophilic aromatic substitution है, और ये aromaticity बचाने के लिए add करने के बजाय substitute करते हैं।
Directive influence एक line में: ortho para activating donors जैसे hydroxyl, amino, और methyl; halogens ortho para लेकिन deactivating; और meta directing deactivators जैसे nitro और carboxyl।
और alkane के दो orders अलग रखो: halogen reactivity fluorine, chlorine से बड़ा, chlorine, bromine से, bromine, iodine से; hydrogen replacement tertiary, secondary से बड़ा, secondary, primary से।
और chapter से साथ ले जाने वाले mnemonics: staggered मतलब spread मतलब stable; B r breaks the rule; और aromatic substitutes, never adds।
